item.title: Operations Manager (Facilities/IT and Fleet)
item.description: Join Rainbow Trust Children’s Charity and play a vital role in ensuring our teams can support families facing the unimaginable, helping us make a real difference. We are looking for an experienced Operations Manager to take operational ownership of IT infrastructure and MSP relationship management, facilities, fleet, and contracts across our organisation. This is a wide-ranging role where your work directly underpins our frontline teams’ ability to deliver life-changing support to families with seriously ill children. About the role: Reporting directly to the Director of Finance and Operations, you will have input into how Rainbow Trust manages its IT, property and facilities, and fleet - while also leading on the day-to-day operational infrastructure across the organisation, including overall responsibility for our IT infrastructure and security. The role holder will act as the primary internal point of contact for our Managed Service Provider, overseeing service delivery, SLAs, and ensuring our IT infrastructure remains secure, compliant and fit for purpose Managing the office facilities, leases, and contracts across our head office and nine regional sites, you will lead on contract negotiation and supplier management, managing a central administration budget and project manage office moves and operational projects. With a focus on improving the efficiency of our systems, processes and ways of working, you will also line manage our Fleet Administrator, overseeing our fleet of 80 leased vehicles and be an integral part of decision making. This is a substantive management role with real ownership, and meaningful variety - ideal for an experienced operations professional with a sound understanding of Microsoft Administration and cyber security ready to take on a broad remit in a values-driven organisation. What we’re looking for: Applications will be particularly welcome from those who have demonstrable experience of negotiating and managing contracts, including managed IT service contracts and budgets. A qualification in cyber security or IT and experience of Microsoft administration, cyber security and MSP management is also necessary for this role. A systematic and effective problem solver – you are self-disciplined and analytical, and you thrive on providing solutions, delivering high standards, and are skilled in appropriately tailoring your output to a range of different stakeholders for decision-making. A self-disciplined multi-tasker who is able to work independently and at a fast pace to meet deadlines – you are someone who perseveres and ensures close follow-up of delegated tasks to deliver consistently high-quality work through to completion. A strong verbal and written communicator with a high level of attention to detail –you’re a quick decision maker, who operates well within a defined area of control, basing your decisions on policy and procedures. You build strong working relationships both internally and externally – you are driven to achieve results and have the ability to train and support others to make correct decisions You work well within established systems, standards and procedures – you are accurate, highly numerate with excellent Excel skills and make fact-based and solution orientated decisions. Why join us? We’re proud to be a Two-Star Best Companies Top 50 mid-sized organisation and a Top 10 Charity, and we’re committed to creating a great place to work. You will benefit from: Pension scheme where we contribute 5% of your salary and you contribute at least 3%. Flexible working hours to balance home and working life. 25 days of annual leave plus public holidays – rising to 26 days after 1 year, 27 days after 5 years and 30 days after 11 years, with an additional 5 days to use in your 10th or 20th year of service (pro rata for part time). The option to buy/sell annual leave, as well as additional leave for your birthday, wedding/civil ceremony and an extra half day off for Christmas shopping. Time off in Lieu. Employee Assistance Programme with access to remote GP, counselling, physiotherapy, resources to support your mental health and financial wellbeing, as well as a 24/7 helpline via Help@Hand. Family friendly policies, focused on employee wellbeing, and an active cross-organisational wellbeing group running a number of initiatives throughout the year. Access to the Blue Light Card Scheme, and other rewards and discounts. Bike to work, season ticket loan and payroll giving schemes. A recommend a friend recruitment bonus scheme. Robust training and development programmes to support your learning and growth. If you’d like to find out more about these benefits and working with us, please visit our why work with us page. More information about us and our recruitment process can be found in our online Candidate Pack. About us: Rainbow Trust Children’s Charity enables families who have a child with a life-threatening or terminal illness to make the most of time together, providing expert, practical and emotional support, where they need it for as long as it is needed. For families living with childhood illness, time is everything. Right now, there are too many families coping alone with no support, no time to think, no time to make memories and no time for each other. We believe that no family should go through this alone, so we are here to change that. Apply now: To apply please send your CV and Covering letter to us via the link. Your covering letter should highlight why your application should be considered above others and clearly state how your experience matches the essential criteria outlined in the Person Specification. For a full job description and person specification please visit our website Please disclose in your covering letter if you have used AI for any part of your job application. Early application is encouraged as we will review applications throughout the advertising period and reserve the right to close the advert early. Interviews will take place at our Head Office in Leatherhead. We will only contact those applicants who have been successful. If you require any adjustments during the interview process, please let us know. An enhanced DBS disclosure will be required for this post. Rainbow Trust is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expects all employees to share this commitment. Rainbow Trust is an equal opportunities employer, and we welcome applications from all backgrounds.
item.dc:creator: Rainbow Trust Children's Charity

item.title: Societies Development Coordinator
item.description: Students’ Union UCL is an organisation that exists to make more happen. We are the representative body for University College London’s (UCL) students, one of the most diverse student communities in the world. Our vision is to provide an outstanding experience for all UCL students and to be one of the best students’ unions in the UK and the world. We aim to build a vibrant and empowered student community with real influence in UCL and beyond, that enables students to enjoy their time at university; pursue their interests and passions; see the world in new ways; and develop the skills and experience to change the world for the better. We are a registered charity employing over 150 career staff and 300 student staff, delivering a wide range of services and representative functions for UCL students. We have the widest portfolio of services of any student organisation in the country, managing UCL’s extracurricular programmes for sport, music, drama, dance, media, volunteering, academic societies and intercultural engagement; providing a wide range of fantastic social spaces; leading on student democracy and representation across UCL; and offering excellent student support services. It's an exciting time to join our growing organisation as we lead the delivery of UCL’s ground-breaking Student Life Strategy. This is enabling us to build more programmes to improve students’ mental and physical wellbeing, promote genuine equity for all, build students’ skills and confidence, develop their international connections and intercultural skills, and make a real contribution to our local community. The role is a permanent contract. This role is based at our Bloomsbury campus with flexibility to work from home on a 40/60 basis (40% working from the office). We will consider applications to work on a part-time, flexible, and job share basis wherever possible. Do you have experience in organising and managing a variety of events; or enabling volunteers to deliver events? Do you have Knowledge and understanding of student activities programmes including clubs, societies and volunteering? If the answer is yes, then we want to hear from you. Our ideal candidate will have the ability to manage conflicting priorities and busy workload, excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to work with a diverse range of people and be committed to working in a democratic and student led environment.
item.dc:creator: Students' Union UCL

item.title: Disability Employment Coach (Part Time)
item.description: 10–12 hours per week | £10,582–£12,698 per annum pro rata (£37,037 FTE) | Fixed term for 5 years to July 2031 | 3% pension CHOICE IN HACKNEY is looking for an experienced and motivated Disability Employment Coach to support disabled people to move towards employment, volunteering, education and training, while developing the confidence, skills and practical strategies needed for sustainable employment. You will provide one-to-one employment coaching, helping participants identify their strengths, aspirations and goals and develop personalised action plans. You will support people to overcome barriers to employment through practical coaching, encouragement, problem-solving and appropriate signposting. You will also help plan and deliver CHOICE IN HACKNEY’s Job Club, creating accessible and engaging sessions that encourage confidence, peer learning and mutual support. Alongside this, you will develop relationships with employers, recruitment agencies, training providers and partner organisations to create opportunities for disabled people. The role recognises that employment can take different forms. You will support participants to explore volunteering, work experience, apprenticeships, self-employment, social enterprise and entrepreneurship where appropriate. You will also provide suitable in-work support to promote job retention, workplace integration and career progression. An important part of the post will be maintaining contact with programme alumni, monitoring longer-term employment, training and wellbeing outcomes and contributing to an active alumni network offering Job Club activities, peer support, mentoring and employer engagement. We are looking for someone with experience supporting disabled people into employment, education or training, together with experience of employment coaching, careers guidance, employability support or vocational rehabilitation. You will need excellent coaching and motivational skills, an understanding of disability and barriers to employment, and knowledge of reasonable adjustments and inclusive recruitment. CHOICE IN HACKNEY is a Disabled People’s Organisation committed to the Social Model of Disability, equality, inclusion and independent living, and welcomes applications from disabled people and people with lived experience.
item.dc:creator: Choice in Hackney

item.title: VCSE Development Coach
item.description: It’s an exciting time at Nova with new innovative projects that will support local good causes. We are a small Wakefield-based charity with a big impact for community groups, charities and social enterprises across the district. We do this through networks, funding, advocacy and specialist advice – that’s where you could come in. We’re looking for someone to join our friendly and collaborative team following a recent review of priorities and role. Someone that is passionate about working with the diverse range of Voluntary, Community and Social Enterprise (VCSE) organisations who create positive change in local communities. Support from our team helps 6 in 10 members to grow and develop, so it’s a fantastic way to use your skills to make a lasting impact. What does this role involve? The Coach will help VCSE organisations build confidence, strengthen their organisations and achieve their goals. They’ll do this by: · Providing one-to-one guidance · Supporting the start-up of new organisations · Providing funding information and support with bid writing · Designing and delivering training · Connecting organisations with the right resources and networks What are we looking for in our VCSE Development Coach? · Experience of supporting groups and organisations to achieve their goals · Understanding of the value of VCSE organisations · Experience of working directly with people, building positive relationships and trust · Awareness of organisational structures, finances, and income generation · Excellent interpersonal, communication and digital skills · A willingness to develop specialist VCSE sector knowledge Take a look at the Person Specification on our website for more details and if you feel you are the right person, we’d encourage you to apply! We value personal qualities and experience as well as work experience. What do we offer? You’ll benefit from a competitive salary, 28 days a holiday a year (plus bank holidays), and some great benefits including: · Blended home and office working · Flexible working hours · Employee Assistance Programme · Staff Rewards Programme · 5% salary contribution to a pension scheme · A range of enhanced policies and practices to ensure a supportive and inclusive workplace · Annual pay reviews We’re an equal opportunities organisation and invite applications from all sections of the community. It’s important to us that everyone is welcomed and valued in our workplace, so we support staff and applicants in a number of ways. More information can be found on our website and in our Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Statement. To apply, visit our website and complete the online application form. Closing date : Friday 11 September at 5pm Interview dates : Thursday 24 and Tuesday 29 September We notify all applicants of the outcome of your application however, due to capacity, we are unable to provide feedback to applicants until the interview stage.

item.title: Partnership Coordinator
item.description: Partnership Coordinator Salary: £28,860 per annum (subject to an annual salary review) Contract: Fixed-term for 12 months (possibility of a contract extension / change to a permanent contract in the future subject to funding and business need) Start Date: As soon as possible (specific date to be agreed with consideration for your notice period) Location: This is a blended-working role with two days per week at our office in Finsbury Park (Tuesday-Thursday) during term time and the flexibility to work from home during school holidays. Occasional travel to schools and events will be required. Working Pattern : 37.5 hours per week. Our core hours are 09:30 - 16:00 from Monday to Friday. About the Role The Partnership Coordinator role is varied, offering the chance to develop a wide range of skills. Responsibilities include managing local Hubs, delivering programme and network activities, supporting events and meetings, and participating in recruitment and retention activities. Working closely with school and trust leaders and Hub Managers, you will need excellent relationship management skills, attention to detail, and a commitment to continuous improvement. Strong evaluation and data management skills would also be an advantage. This position requires individuals who are self-motivated, organised, detail-focused, and strong communicators. We are looking for a new colleague to focus on account managing some of our local Hubs, and supporting recruitment and retention of schools and trusts. This would account for about 60-80% of your time. The remaining time will be spent on delivering our programmes and networks, ensuring a great experience for our partner schools, supporting knowledge exchange, and handling general partner queries. Key Responsibilities Reporting to the Partnership Experience Manager, the Partnership Coordinator will have the following key areas of responsibility and will be expected to undertake other responsibilities commensurate with the role as requested: Programme and Network Delivery Provide year-round support to local Hub Managers to ensure schools receive necessary support. Maintain relationships with key stakeholders, including resolving operational issues and escalating as needed. Support the planning and delivery of programmes and networks, including scheduling dates, organising training sessions, and other activities. Support the organisation and delivery of programme-specific and national events. Partner Relationship Management Work with the Challenge Partners Central Team to ensure an excellent experience for partners and help schools maximise their partnership value. Support the induction and onboarding of new schools to their Hubs and the National Network of Excellence. Troubleshoot and respond to school or trust queries through internal customer care systems. Utilise and update our CRM system (Salesforce). Data Management Monitor, consolidate and analyse programme, network and Hub data to identify risks and/or trends, providing regular reports and updates to support the continuous improvement of our activities. Utilise our CRM system (Salesforce) to build reporting efficiencies. Communications Respond to email and phone queries about Challenge Partners, programmes, networks, and Hubs professionally and promptly. Collaborate with programme, network, and partnership leads to provide high-quality communications to partner schools, including renewals, induction, onboarding, engagement emails, and Hub updates. Play a leading role in the delivery of the half termly Partnership newsletter, using data to evaluate engagement and make further improvements. Recruitment and Retention Support year-round recruitment of schools to the Network of Excellence, working with hubs to deliver introductory events. Provide updates on schools in your Hub to inform retention campaigns. Manage leads and connect new schools with local Hubs. Support the tracking of sign-ups throughout the recruitment period, providing regular data updates to the wider team. General Responsibilities Champion Challenge Partners’ vision, values, and commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion. Take ownership of personal development and actively contribute to team learning. Maintain high standards of health, safety, and welfare for yourself and others. Attend events and external meetings, which may require travel and occasional overnight stays. Person Specification

item.title: EA to CEO and Governance
item.description: Executive Assistant to the CEO and Governance Salary: £40,000 per annum, pro rata Hours: 28 hours per week Location: Hybrid, London-based with occasional travel to central London We're seeking an organised and proactive Executive Assistant to support our CEO and help ensure effective governance across a national charity. This is a varied role combining executive support, board administration, governance coordination, risk management and event planning. Working closely with senior leaders and trustees, you'll play a key role in helping the organisation achieve its mission and strategic goals. What you'll do Provide high-quality support to the CEO, including diary management, meeting coordination and briefings. Coordinate Board, committee and leadership meetings, including agendas, papers and minutes. Maintain governance records and support compliance requirements. Manage the organisational risk register and support policy reviews. Organise AGMs, away days and staff events. Build strong relationships with trustees, colleagues and external stakeholders. About you You'll bring: Significant executive or senior administrative support experience in a charity. Experience supporting governance processes, boards or committees. The ability to manage confidential information with discretion and professionalism. Proficiency in Microsoft 365 and related collaboration tools. Join us and help create the strong foundations that enable a mission-driven organisation to thrive. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and experiences and are committed to building an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. We want you to have every opportunity to demonstrate your skills, ability and potential; please contact us if you require any assistance or adjustment so that we can help with making the application process work for you. item.title: Immigration Caseworker: Part time
item.description: Immigration Caseworker Hours: 3 days per week (21 hrs) Salary range: £16,500-18,456 pro rata (£27,500-£30,670 FTE) Place of work: Hybrid Benefits: • Flexible and hybrid working arrangements. • Training and professional development opportunities. • Study leave to support accreditation progression. • The opportunity to make a meaningful difference to the lives of refugees, asylum seekers and migrants. • Supportive working environment within a small and committed charity. About us Wanstead and Woodford Migrant Support provides immigration advice and practical support to refugees, asylum seekers and migrants across North East London and Essex. We are a small charity committed to ensuring that people can access high quality advice, support and advocacy regardless of their circumstances. About the role We are seeking a qualified Immigration Caseworker to join our growing service. This is an exciting opportunity to work within a small and supportive organisation delivering high-quality immigration advice and casework to migrants, refugees and asylum seekers. The role is primarily home-based, with attendance required at outreach locations, meetings and occasional events. The successful candidate will manage their own caseload, provide immigration advice within their accreditation level and contribute to the development of the charity's advice service. Applicants Applicants must hold IAA Level 1 or Level 2 accreditation (or IAAS equivalent). Candidates holding Level 1 accreditation will be expected to work towards Level 2 accreditation within an agreed timeframe. Appropriate supervision, training and study leave will be provided to support progression. Salary progression will be linked to the achievement of higher accreditation levels in accordance with the charity's pay structure. How to apply Please click on the link below. You will be asked to answer three questions and upload your CV. The closing deadline is 25 September.

item.title: Academy Stewardship Officer
item.description: Working with colleagues across the Academy, Marketing and Communications, and wider teams, this new role is responsible for growing and nurturing engaged Academy audiences across online communities, social media, email and other channels. The role will plan, draft and publish approved content; moderate and manage online groups in line with community guidelines; and support the promotion of Academy learning opportunities through case studies, testimonials, photography and video content. By monitoring audience growth, engagement and retention, maintaining accurate records and ensuring use of content is compliant with Battersea privacy and retention policies, the role will help demonstrate the impact of the Academy and support its ambition to reach, engage and benefit more organisations, individuals and animals. What we can offer you: In return for your commitment to our cause and to recognise the value of our employees, Battersea offers a range of benefits to support the wellbeing of our employees. These include: 28 days of annual leave (plus 8 days paid public holidays) per year. Discounted gym memberships and cycle to work schemes. Employee Assistance Programme and access to Wellbeing Resources. Generous pension contributions - up to 10% employer contribution. Free healthcare cash plan, where you can claim for a range of treatment including dental, optical, physiotherapy, chiropody and acupuncture every year. Annual interest-free season ticket loans. We are also committed to providing learning and development to our employees. During your time with us, we provide support for your professional and career development, including access to digital and in-person training programmes, leadership and management training, mentoring and much more. Diversity and inclusion: We are committed to providing a welcoming and inclusive experience for all staff, volunteers and trustees and those hoping to join us. We operate an anonymised shortlisting process and actively seek to ensure our process is fair and equitable for all. We understand the value of diverse voices, perspectives, and experiences to help us deliver even more for our dogs and cats, and we welcome applicants from all sections of the community. As a Disability Confident Committed Employer we will ask about any adjustments you may need at application and/or interview stage, and if you are offered a role with us, we’ll talk to you about any workplace adjustments you may need to help you perform at your best. If you would like to talk more about this, please contact us. Greyscale copies of the recruitment pack are also available on request. More about us: At Battersea, we aim to never turn away a dog or cat in need of help. We give each one lots of love, expert care and get to know their characters and quirks so we can find them a new home that’s just right for them. Join us and help us be here for every dog and cat, wherever they are, for as long as they need us. Acceptable use of AI: At Battersea, we value expertise. We recognise each candidate that applies to us will have a range of expertise they can offer us, so we want to hear about this in your own words. We understand the support that generative artificial intelligence (AI) software can offer but it can also lead to numerous applications presenting as generic and impersonal. This makes it difficult to gain understanding of your unique experience. To best showcase yourself, we encourage you to write your responses without the assistance of AI. If you require the use of AI software to aid in completing your application, we ask you use the generative responses as a prompt for writing your answers and avoid copying and pasting. You must also ensure the information presented in your application accurately reflects your experience. Closing date : Sunday 13th September 2026, 11.59pm All applications must be submitted before the closing date advertised. We reserve the right to close the vacancy early if a high volume of applications is received. Interview date(s) : Friday 18th September 2026 For more information about the role, please download our Recruitment pack. To apply for the role, please click the "Apply" button below.

item.title: Finance & Administrative Officer
item.description: Job description We are looking for a conscientious Finance & Administration Officer , to join our Finance team on a one-year maternity contract. You will process financial transactions, maintain accurate records, reconcile accounts and support month-end and annual reporting activities. You will work closely with the Head of Finance, Financial Accountant and wider Secretariat teams to ensure effective financial administration and compliance. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced finance administrator or finance officer looking to develop their career within a respected humanitarian organisation. About you We're looking for someone who combines strong financial administration skills with excellent attention to detail and a collaborative approach. You must be detail-oriented with a zeal to support the financial backbone of the secretariat. You must demonstrate strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with a proven ability to manage multiple priorities. Some of the key criterion for this role include: Experience in processing invoices and handling supplier payment queries. Experience of bank, cash and credit card reconciliations. Experience using finance systems and reporting tools Understanding of accounting and bookkeeping procedures. Knowledge of charity finance processes and compliance. Previous administrative experience in a busy office environment, being proactive and demonstrating excellent organisational and time-management skills, to manage competing priorities. Excellent attention to detail and accuracy. Strong Excel skills and confidence working with financial data. Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications. Strong written and verbal communication skills. ***Please download the job description for full details*** The DEC is committed to the safeguarding and protection of children and vulnerable adults and participates in the Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. In line with this Scheme, we will request information from successful applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. Posted on: 24 August 2026 Closing date: 07 September 2026 at 18:00 Job ref: Finance & Administrative Officer (maternity cover) Tags: Administration, Finance, International Development, Accounting, Humanitarian Aid, Procurement, Statutory The client requests no contact from agencies or media sales.

item.title: Volunteer Coordinator
item.description: 10 hours per week | £10,067 per annum pro rata (£35,235 FTE) | Fixed term for 1 year, with possibility of extension | 3% pension CHOICE IN HACKNEY is looking for an enthusiastic and organised Volunteer Coordinator to develop and coordinate our volunteering programme and support a diverse team of volunteers across the organisation. You will recruit, induct, train, place and supervise volunteers, including gardeners, befrienders and administrative assistants. You will also support disabled people who want to volunteer, helping them develop their confidence, skills and employment prospects through meaningful volunteering opportunities. A key part of the role will be matching volunteers with disabled people living in the community. You will assess individual needs, skills, interests, experience and availability to create appropriate and rewarding placements. You will maintain regular contact with volunteers and service users, review placement arrangements, support individual care plans and resolve any issues that arise. The role also involves maintaining accurate records, gathering feedback, producing reports and working with managers to identify new volunteering opportunities. You will recruit and support a Volunteer Fundraiser and help develop community fundraising initiatives. We are looking for someone with experience of recruiting and supervising volunteers or staff, supporting disabled people who may be at risk, organising services or projects, administration and partnership working. You will need excellent communication and organisational skills, the ability to motivate volunteers and manage competing priorities, and a good understanding of safeguarding, equality and inclusion. CHOICE IN HACKNEY is a Disabled People’s Organisation committed to the Social Model of Disability, equality, inclusion and independent living, and welcomes applications from disabled people and people with lived experience.

item.title: Business Support and Project Coordinator
item.description: CPRE was set up 100 years ago with the aims of the ‘conservation of what is beautiful and interesting in our countryside and towns and villages; and the encouragement of the right type of development’. Today these words are just as relevant as when they were written in the 1920s and we campaign for good planning, protection from speculative development, and the enhancement of nature and accessibility of our green spaces. CPRE Oxfordshire is an independent charity, federated with 40+ county charities and a national office, giving us local, regional and national reach. Reporting to the Director, the Business Support and Project Coordinator will work to ensure the smooth operation of the Branch office and administrative systems and support coordination of projects and events. We are looking for a highly motivated and dynamic individual who can operate independently but who is also an enthusiastic and effective team player, helping others to work to the best of their ability while ensuring the timely delivery of tasks. As a key member of a small but energetic team, the successful candidate will have the opportunity to deploy their skills across a broad range of areas, building relationships and working with the entire staff team, our District volunteer network, and our Board of Trustees. You will be highly organised with an eye for detail but above all be someone who is resourceful and proactive and enjoys working across multiple areas at the same time. Responsibilities: The Business Support and Project Coordinator is responsible for ensuring the smooth operation of the Branch office and administrative systems and supporting the coordination of projects and events. This includes: 1. Financial management 1.1 Transitioning existing electronic records to a new accounting system 1.2 Recording and processing donations 1.3 Preparing, submitting and tracking Gift Aid claims with HMRC 1.4 Processing monthly payroll, pension and HMRC submissions 1.5 Preparing and managing financial records for funding and expenditure 1.6 Preparing, sending and arranging payment of invoices 2. Branch and office management 2.1 Undertaking general administrative duties, including responding to enquiries, overseeing company insurance, and managing office contracts 2.2 Assisting with IT systems and security (e.g. Microsoft 365, domain renewal) 2.3 Overseeing compliance with Data Protection regulations and requirements (general knowledge required) 2.4 Assisting Trustees, Staff and Volunteers to ensure compliance with employment, health & safety, HMRC, Charity Commission and Companies House regulations and requirements 2.5 Liaising with National CPRE office on volunteer management and recruitment 2.6 Assisting the Trustees and Director with induction of new employees 2.7 Assisting the Director with preparation of induction packs for new District, Branch and Office Volunteers 3. Events and project coordination 3.1 Supporting Trustee, Staff and Volunteer attendance at external events 3.2 Supporting the Branch Director with the organisation and delivery of events focused on membership growth, volunteer recruitment, and fundraising 3.3 Supporting the Branch Director with the coordination and delivery of projects, to include contract development, basic monitoring and reporting, payment of contractors 4. Membership management 4.1 Updating National membership records 4.2 Occasional distribution of membership records to Districts 4.3 Supporting National CPRE office in sending out welcome packs and consents 4.4 Updating mailing lists for AGMs, Branch and District materials, etc 5. Contact management 5.1 Developing and maintaining Branch records for District Chairs, President, Vice Presidents, Consultants and other Volunteers 5.2 Developing and maintaining wider Branch contact records, e.g. Media, MPs, partner CEOs, local authority staff and elected officials, donors, trusts and foundations We’re committed to creating an inclusive and diverse workplace at CPRE, not just because it’s the right thing to do, but because diverse workplaces can make better and more creative decisions. Whatever your background, we welcome your application. To apply, please provide your CV and a covering letter explaining how you meet the requirements of the post. Closing date for applications is Monday 14 September 2026. Interviews will be held week commencing 21 September 2026. Please note: Applicants must have the right to work in the UK. We do not accept CVs or applications via recruitment agencies.
item.dc:creator: Campaign to Protect Rural England (CPRE) Oxfordshire

item.title: Member Support & Administrative Assistant
item.description: We are seeking a self-motivated Member Support and Administrative Assistant to play a key role in our friendly team. The successful candidate will liaise with colleagues across the organisation focused on membership, communications, marketing and delivery, and as a result get invaluable insight into these functions. Once established in post the successful candidate will also benefit from our nine-day fortnight working pattern (providing a long weekend twice a month). B a c k gr oun d Information PSHE (personal, social, health and economic) education is the school curriculum subject that prepares pupils for life and work. PSHE lessons cover some of the most pressing issues facing young people today including mental and physical health, relationships, staying safe online, economic wellbeing, careers and the importance of equality and diversity. The PSHE Association is the national body for the subject. A charity and membership organisation, the Association supports a national network of over 50,000 teachers and schools with resources, training and guidance. We work nationally to raise PSHE standards for all children and raise its status on the curriculum. This includes working in partnership with a range of leading charities, government bodies, corporates and other partners. This is an exciting time for us and we are expanding our services to meet growing demand. Role description The applicant will be expected to take on a variety of responsibilities associated with supporting our national membership of PSHE education teachers and other professionals. This will include fielding phone and emailed member queries in a timely and friendly fashion and logging queries and activities on our membership database. The role will also include supporting the organisation and administration of the office, including processing memberships and payments, and maintaining and updating our database of contacts, supporting online training event bookings and logistics as well as supporting the team as required. Please see below for a full Job Description and Person Specification T e r ms of Reference The post is offered on a full time basis, on a permanent contract with a six-month probationary period. The salary will be £28,500. At the PSHE Association, we believe in a healthy work-life balance. That is why we offer a nine-day fortnight working pattern, giving our team every other Friday off (in other words a long weekend twice a month). We believe this gives employees more time to recharge and more time for what matters to them. This shorter working week benefit (equivalent to 32 hours per week on full pay) kicks in once employees have successfully completed three months of their probationary period, with a standard 35-hour working week in place up until that point. Our offices are based in central London, close to Russell Square, and this is where the role will be primarily based alongside some days of the week working from home. How to apply To apply please send a CV and covering letter using Charity Job by Monday 7th September at 9AM. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to attend a first round interview on Thursday 17th September on Zoom. There will also potentially be a second round interview held face to face on the week of Monday 21st September in our London office. The cover letter is an important part of the process, and we will not consider any applications without a cover letter attached. This letter should provide an overview and personal reflections about why you meet the criteria and how your skills and experience are applicable. We therefore request that no AI tools are used in its composition.

item.title: Event & Engagement Coordinator
item.description: Event & Engagement Coordinator Remotely based in North West England and a willingness to travel where appropriate Job Purpose: To plan, coordinate, and deliver a range of local events across North West England with the potential to grow into other areas in the future, ensuring each event is well-organised, inclusive, and engaging for local communities. The Local Event & Engagement Coordinator will collaborate closely with partners, local authorities, suppliers, volunteers, and members to deliver high-quality, unique and memorable experiences. Who are we looking for? · Energetic and positive, bringing enthusiasm to everything you do. · Excited by change, seeing new opportunities and possibilities. · Keen to succeed with a strong development mindset. · Passionate about delivering great events and experiences. · Open to feedback, always looking for ways to improve. Key Responsibilities: Event Coordination · Plan and manage logistics for a variety of local member events, making sure all events are accessible and attractive to both existing and potential members. · Liaise with relevant external and internal contacts such as venues, suppliers, CSSC’s ticketing platform, Head Office departments, and volunteers. · Complete all relevant compliance work such as risk assessments and public liability checks. · Support both long standing and new volunteers with all aspects of volunteer led events, including creating events on ticketing platform and promoting events through email and social platforms · Develop and manage event budgets, ensuring value for money and accurate financial tracking. · Oversee event setup and breakdown where applicable, managing on-site logistics and resolving any issues on the day. · Recruit and coordinate volunteers to assist with events. · Evaluate event success through feedback, data collection, and post-event reporting. Digital Engagement · Promote events via social media, email campaigns, posters, and local press in collaboration with marketing teams. · Manage and grow the North West’s CSSC TikTok presence, including content planning, filming, editing, posting, and community engagement. · Create engaging, on-brand short-form video content tailored to target audiences. · Monitor performance metrics and use insights to optimise content strategy and increase reach and engagement. · Stay up to date with emerging social media trends, tools, and platform updates. Key Skills & Experience: Essential: · Proven experience in planning and delivering events. · Strong organisational and time-management skills. · Ability to manage budgets and handle multiple projects simultaneously. · Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills. · Flexibility to work evenings and weekends when required. · Ability to analyse member insights to inform event planning and attract potential new members. · Ability to work collaboratively with regional teams to support membership growth and positive member experiences. · Ability to build rapport with volunteers and identify the support needed for successful event delivery. · Confidence in using IT systems and ticketing platforms to promote events across appropriate channels. Desirable: · Experience working with community groups, charities, membership organisations or not for profits. · Knowledge of health and safety and safeguarding procedures. · Familiarity with marketing or PR for events. · First Aid or event safety training. · Previous experience with ticketing platforms or willingness to learn. · Understanding of how comms and events align with one another. · Data literacy or willingness to understand some basic data analytics · Full UK driving licence and willingness to travel where appropriate

item.title: Data Migration Specialist
item.description: Data Migration Specialist Amnesty International UK (AIUK) 6 month FTC £48,599 per annum FTC Full time, 35 hours per week Remote/ Hybrid, minimum once a month - London based (WC1X) Role closing - 3 rd September Interviews: 16 th September Charity People are thrilled to be supporting Amnesty International UK to find them an interim Data Migration Specialist to play a critical role in delivering one of their most significant data and technology projects in their history. Amnesty International UK (AIUK) is part of a global movement campaigning for a world where everyone can enjoy their human rights, live free from fear and be treated with dignity and equality. Independent of governments, political parties and commercial interests, Amnesty works alongside communities worldwide to challenge injustice, expose human rights abuses and campaign for meaningful change. Powered by the support of hundreds of thousands of members and supporters, Amnesty stands up for justice, freedom, and equality wherever they are under threat. AIUK are undertaking a major digital transformation programme that will shape how they campaign, engage supporters, raise funds and fight for human rights across the globe. You will be joining AIUK's Data, Digital and Technology Transformation team, you will take ownership of key migration activities across extraction, cleansing, transformation, loading, and validation. Acting as a technical lead for migration workstreams, you will collaborate with colleagues, suppliers, and stakeholders to ensure data quality remains at the heart of every decision. This role has a strong benefit of flexible working hours fortnightly. You will be expected to travel to the offices for the first few days for induction and then a minimum of once a month thereafter. Key responsibilities: Leading end-to-end data migration activities across development, testing, and production environments Extracting and analysing data from legacy systems using SQL Designing complex cross-system mappings and transformation rules Identifying and resolving data quality issues, anomalies, and inconsistencies Creating migration datasets, reconciliation reports, and validation processes Maintaining migration documentation, technical runbooks, and mapping specifications Providing technical guidance and quality assurance support to colleagues and stakeholders Supporting migration cutover planning and execution You will bring: Significant experience using SQL for complex data extraction and selection activities Strong expertise in data migration principles, methodologies, and best practice Experience designing and delivering large-scale cross-system data mappings A track record of leading data cleansing, standardisation, and transformation activities Experience working with CRM platforms, ideally within the not-for-profit sector Knowledge of payment processing, including Direct Debits and Gift Aid Desirable experience includes Salesforce for Nonprofits, FinDock, Agile delivery environments and recognised data migration certifications. This is an opportunity to combine your technical expertise with meaningful purpose, ensuring that the data underpinning Amnesty's work is accurate, accessible, and ready to support their next generation CRM platform. You will be a data professional who enjoys solving complex problems, improving data quality, and delivering successful migration outcomes in challenging environments. If you are keen to apply, please do apply without delay and we shall be back in touch asap. Charity People actively promotes equality, diversity and inclusion. We match charity needs with the skills and experience of candidates, irrespective of age, disability (including hidden disabilities), gender, gender identity or gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, or sexual orientation. We do this because we know greater diversity will lead to even greater results for the charities we work with.
item.dc:creator: Charity People

item.title: Fundraising Officer
item.description: The Centre for ADHD and Autism Support (CAAS) is looking for a passionate, proactive and relationship-focused Fundraising Officer to help grow our income and expand our impact across North West London. Every year, CAAS supports hundreds of ADHD and autistic children, young people, adults and their families through information, advice, support services, training and community programmes. As demand for our services continues to grow, we are seeking a talented fundraiser who can help us build strong supporter relationships, develop new income streams, and ensure our vital work reaches even more people. If you are an experienced fundraiser who enjoys building connections, creating opportunities and making a real difference in your community, we'd love to hear from you. Location: Eastcote, HA4 9XA (with some potential for home working) Salary: £30,000 FTE (£17,015 pro rata, inclusive of holiday allowance) Hours: 23 hours per week during term time (38 weeks) plus 7 hours per week for 6 weeks during school holidays Reports to: Fundraising & Communications Manager About the Role Working closely with the Fundraising & Communications Manager and CEO, you will play a key role in developing and delivering fundraising activities that generate sustainable income and increase awareness of CAAS. This varied and rewarding role will include: Developing and delivering community fundraising initiatives and events Recruiting and supporting individual and community fundraisers Building relationships with donors, schools, community groups and corporate partners Researching and developing new fundraising opportunities Supporting trust and grant applications Helping to grow digital and social media fundraising campaigns Maintaining fundraising records and supporter data using our CRM Representing CAAS at events, presentations and community engagements You will also act as an ambassador for the charity, delivering excellent supporter care and helping donors understand the impact of their contributions. About You We're looking for someone who brings enthusiasm, initiative and a proven ability to generate income through fundraising activities. You will have: Essential Experience in a fundraising role, ideally within the charity or not-for-profit sector A successful track record in community fundraising, events, individual giving or related income generation Experience building relationships with donors, supporters, community groups or corporate partners Strong communication and presentation skills Excellent written skills, including experience preparing funding applications or fundraising materials Experience using a CRM or database to manage supporter information Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities A positive, professional and collaborative approach Desirable Experience supporting fundraising volunteers or volunteer groups Corporate fundraising experience Experience contributing to larger trust and foundation applications Knowledge of digital fundraising and social media campaigns A fundraising qualification or equivalent experience Full UK driving licence You do not need previous experience of working with ADHD or autistic people. Full training will be provided. What matters most is that you share our commitment to inclusion, diversity and improving the lives of neurodivergent people and their families. Why Join CAAS? Make a genuine difference to local families and communities Join a passionate and supportive team Flexible working arrangements available Opportunity to develop your fundraising career across multiple income streams Training and professional development opportunities Be part of a respected charity with a growing impact across North West London Our Commitment to Equality, Diversity and Inclusion CAAS values diversity and welcomes applications from people of all backgrounds. We particularly encourage applications from people from Black, Asian and ethnic minority communities, disabled people, and LGBTQ+ candidates. We are committed to flexible working and will consider options including term-time working, compressed hours, annualised hours and job-share arrangements where appropriate. Safeguarding CAAS is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults. The successful candidate will be required to provide satisfactory references, complete pre-employment checks and undertake an Enhanced DBS check. Apply Now Join us and help create neurodiverse-aware communities where ADHD and autistic people can thrive. If you’re looking for a supportive, inclusive workplace, we’d be delighted to receive your application, along with a short covering note. Please note If you haven’t heard from us within two weeks of the closing date, please assume that you have not been shortlisted for interview. Due to the volume of applications we receive, we are unfortunately unable to respond to everyone individually. Thank you for considering a role with us – we genuinely value your interest and hope you will consider applying for future opportunities.

item.title: Fundraising Executive, Giving Campaigns & Products
item.description: About Us The National Trust for Scotland is Scotland’s leading conservation and membership charity dedicated to protecting and promoting Scotland's natural, cultural and built heritage. We care for historic places, landscapes and collections across the country so they can be enjoyed for generations to come. The National Trust for Scotland is a fundraising charity with a successful and high performing fundraising team. Investment and organisational commitment since 2019/20 have driven strong and sustained growth, with the team consistently exceeding targets and generating an average of £10 million annually. Job Purpose The wider purpose of the role is to help drive the National Trust for Scotland’s ability to conserve Scotland’s built, natural and cultural heritage in our care. Specific to this role, you will work with the Fundraising Manager, Giving Campaigns & Products, to grow support and income from individual giving programmes and fundraising products. This is a varied and complex role through which you will support the strategic leadership of mass market and mid-level fundraising, growing our portfolio of donors and prospects and empowering our property teams and supporter groups to raise funds. Coordinating and supporting individual giving programmes and fundraising products such as the Founders’ Circle, regular giving programme, Scottish Heritage Lottery and Dedicate a Tree, you will contribute to achieving an income target of £800,000 and above per year, ensuring vital funds and growing awareness for our charity’s work. A team player, you will work as a key member of the Giving Campaigns & Products team whilst supporting the wider Fundraising & Philanthropy team. This role supports and drives our highest profile, mass market fundraising activity and crucial pipeline development for Fundraising & Philanthropy income streams, requiring skilled multi-tasking, creativity and a laser focus on continuous improvement and results.

item.title: Interim Digital Analyst
item.description: Digital Analyst – Three-Month Contract The Talent Set is delighted to be partnering with a leading children’s charity to recruit an experienced Digital Analyst for an initial three-month contract. Working across Fundraising and Marketing as part of the wider Insight and Performance function, this role will transform digital data into clear, actionable recommendations that improve supporter engagement, digital performance and fundraising outcomes. This is a hands-on interim opportunity for someone who can quickly understand an existing digital estate, maintain robust analytics and tracking, and provide stakeholders with the insight needed to optimise digital campaigns and supporter journeys. Key responsibilities will include: Analysing performance across websites, digital campaigns and supporter journeys, turning findings into practical recommendations. Taking a multichannel view of performance across paid media, email, social media, organic search and other digital platforms. Maintaining and optimising the charity’s GA4 environment, including events, conversions, explorations and reporting. Implementing and maintaining tracking through Google Tag Manager. Using JavaScript and HTML within Google Tag Manager to implement and troubleshoot tracking solutions. Creating dashboards and performance reporting using Power BI, GA4 and other analytics tools. Using SQL to interrogate and analyse large or complex datasets. Identifying opportunities to improve conversion, engagement, retention and the overall supporter experience. Supporting A/B and multivariate testing and making evidence-based optimisation recommendations. Ensuring digital data collection remains compliant with GDPR and cookie consent requirements. Working closely with colleagues across Insight, Fundraising, Marketing, Digital and Technology. We are looking for someone with: Strong hands-on experience of Google Analytics 4 and Google Tag Manager. Experience implementing and maintaining digital tracking. Working knowledge of JavaScript and HTML. Strong SQL and data analysis skills. Experience producing dashboards and performance reporting, ideally using Power BI. A strong understanding of digital marketing channels and multichannel performance. Experience analysing user or supporter journeys and identifying opportunities for optimisation. The ability to communicate complex analysis clearly to non-technical stakeholders. Availability to start at short notice and make an immediate impact. Experience within a charity, fundraising or supporter-focused organisation would be helpful but is not essential. What's on offer £230-315 per day + daily holiday PAYE Three-month contract Starting next week Interviews Thursday 27th August Hybrid, 2 days onsite, central London How to apply Please apply with an up-to-date CV as soon as possible via the apply now button. Interviews will take place on Thursday, with the successful candidate expected to start next week. item.title: Senior Philanthropy Manager
item.description: Senior Philanthropy Manager Prostate Cancer UK Location: Hybrid – a combination of remote and in-person working at our London Bridge office at least 4 days a month Permanent and full-time role Salary: Band 5 range of £51,250 - £60,250 pa Prostate cancer is the most common cancer in the UK - stealing over 12,000 of our dads, grandads, brothers and friends every year. As the largest men’s health charity in the UK, our ambition is clear: to create a world where no man dies from prostate cancer. And this is how we’re making that happen. We are the biggest public funder of prostate cancer research, investing millions to revolutionise testing, treatment, and care. We’re blazing a trail to a screening programme that could save thousands of lives with regular, accurate tests for all men at risk. And we work tirelessly to spread the word about risk and offer specialist support to people living with the disease. This is an exciting and pivotal moment for high value fundraising at Prostate Cancer UK. Through our £100 million Raise the Game appeal, we are accelerating our progress over the next 5 years, to transform how men and their families navigate prostate cancer. We are now seeking a Senior Philanthropy Manager to be at the heart of this mission – securing and stewarding major gifts that will directly fund life-saving research, drive innovation, and ensure more men receive the right treatment at the right time. You will develop and lead on major donor fundraising, working with some of our most influential supporters to unlock gifts that drive real change. You will also motivate and support a small team of fundraisers, and help them to successfully cultivate their portfolios. About you You will be a highly collaborative major gifts fundraiser with a strong track record of developing and securing high-five-figure and six figure gifts. You’ll thrive in fast-paced, ambitious environments, bringing both strategic thinking and the ability to turn plans into action. A confident communicator, people manager and natural relationship builder, you’ll be adaptable, curious and skilled at building trust and credibility with a wide range of internal and external stakeholders. Experience in health or medical fundraising would be valuable, but not essential. What is essential is your ability to interpret complex, specialist information into compelling funding propositions. Underpinning all of this is your passion for driving positive change and your belief in the power of philanthropy to make a meaningful difference. What we offer Join our team and be part of an award-winning charity. We’ll support you to develop your skills and expertise. We offer a competitive benefits package, including: Generous leave entitlements that increase with service One ‘development day’ a month to use for training or personal development Enhanced contributory pension scheme Life insurance and group income protection Health Cash Plan Life and wellbeing advice and support via our Employee Assistance Programme Discounted gym membership and high street shopping discounts Loans for season tickets or cycles Our commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion At Prostate Cancer UK we’re committed to righting health inequalities across the UK, starting with those faced by Black men. This includes ground-breaking research into Black men's risk and working with communities directly to overcome barriers to the diagnosis and treatment of prostate cancer. To make this happen, we're dedicated to being an inclusive, proactive organisation, as we strive to be Allies to Black communities. We’ll achieve this by advocating and working alongside those communities to promote change. We're also working to be Allies to each other, not only protected groups. In 2024, we launched our New Allyship Training Programme. All colleagues at Prostate Cancer UK will be trained to act and identify as an Ally. We've also signed Business in the Community’s Race at Work Charter, as a dedication to our Black health equity work and wider EDI priorities. As a signatory, we're responsible and accountable for driving positive change. Our people networks We’re continuously learning more about the needs of our colleagues, and have three amazing People Networks, sponsored by our Leadership team: Pride – A safe space where LGBTQ+ colleagues – and our allies – can share their diverse lived experiences, celebrate LGBTQ+ culture and history, and create new ideas about how our organisation can be more inclusive and representative of LGBTQ+ people Mind and Body – Here to increase awareness, promote wellbeing and support colleagues affected by neurodiversity, mental health problems, disability and long-term illness Culture Club – Here to increase awareness and celebrate the different cultures and beliefs that we have in the organisation, so that we all have our cultures felt and feel welcomed This is a career defining opportunity to work with us and you’ll see your efforts pay off as we give men and their families the power to navigate prostate cancer. We are partnering with Richmond Associates for this search. To request a copy of the candidate information pack or to apply, please visit their website by following the Application button or contact Nicola Reames, Senior Consultant or Laura Sears, Consultant. Closing date for applications is 9AM TUESDAY, 22 SEPTEMBER 2026 Interviews are currently scheduled to take place from early October 2026.
item.dc:creator: Prostate Cancer UK

item.title: Complex Needs Caseworker
item.description: Complex Needs Caseworker Reading £33,797 - £37,563 pa Are you a creative person looking for role where you can make a lasting difference to people experiencing homelessness in Reading? We are looking for 2 Complex Caseworkers to join our Rough Sleeper team in Reading who provide intensive support to people with complex needs experiencing homelessness. This passionate team offer person centred support service to help people who require a specialist intervention approach to support them through the transition from rough sleeping into sustainable accommodation. We currently have 2 opportunities available: Supporting women experiencing homelessness, including those affected by violence against women and girls (VAWG). Supporting a mixed cohort of clients experiencing homelessness with complex needs. In both roles you will work collaboratively with the Rough Sleeper Navigator Coordinator and Outreach team as well as relevant partner agencies in Reading to deliver sustainable outcomes to clients. You will advocate for clients who have been some of the most marginalised in the local area, to make a real and long lasting difference to their recovery. You will be responsible for overseeing a caseload of clients and providing day to day support to clients with their transition from the streets into accommodation and independent living with a strong focus on tenancy sustainment and rescue. This includes working with people on health, housing, employment and training support. You will be given support to build strong relationships with a range of other services to find creative and sustainable routes to recovery for clients. You’re typical working hours will be Monday – Friday, with flexibility to work outside of these hours at times to support the team through SWEP. About you Above all we are looking for people who share our values; who are passionate about supporting our clients to sustain their recovery. Even if you don’t think you match 100 % of the criteria, we would still like to hear from you as we value transferable skills. Potential can be equally as important as experience, so if you think you have what it takes, please do apply! If you have good communication skills, with the ability to network and build effective relationships with a variety of people, You should have a good working understanding of supporting vulnerable with complex needs, such as substance use, mental and physical health issues, and the ability to understand the difficulties they experience in accessing services that full meet their needs. We will provide you with support, supervision and training so that you can develop the necessary skills to offer a high quality service to clients. Closing date: 10am on 7 September 2026 Interview and assessments on 15-16 September 2026 St Mungo's are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. We strongly encourage applications from all under-represented groups.

item.title: Crisis Recovery Worker
item.description: An exciting part time opportunity has opened up at CPSL Mind. CPSL Mind is a vibrant, values-led charity that supports local people in their recovery from mental health issues, promotes wellbeing and campaigns against stigma and discrimination. Part Time Crisis Recovery Worker Salary: £29,347.00 per annum, FTE Salary Scale Point: 19 (Including 1 point for anti-social hours) Based: The Sanctuary, Peterborough Hours: 42 hours per fortnight, working on a rolling 2 week rota Week 1: Wednesday, Saturday, Sunday Week 2: Tuesday, Thursday, Friday (Evenings Shifts: 4.30pm – 11.30pm) About CPSL Mind Cambridgeshire, Peterborough and South Lincolnshire (CPSL) Mind is a progressive and expanding mental health charity. Our vision is a society in which everyone has positive mental health and feels part of a connected community. Our work ranges from prevention and early intervention to award-winning crisis support. We also seek to influence positive change through our training services and ground-breaking campaigns activity. About the Service The Sanctuary is a non-clinical, safe space for individuals to visit as an alternative to attending A&E and is part of the wider First Response Service across Cambridgeshire and Peterborough. Working one to one (either face to face, over the telephone, or on video call) you will support individuals experiencing mental health distress by: Establishing connection and rapport in a non-intrusive, non-judgmental and compassionate manner Supporting individuals through guided self-help strategies including grounding, breathing techniques. Supporting individuals to relay their immediate needs and concerns and offering emotional and practical support and information to address these. Provide individuals with information on and how to connect with social support networks available to them in their own community. Supporting individuals to make a safety plan Crisis Recovery Worker criteria: You must be able to show empathy and compassion with a non-judgemental approach You should be passionate about promoting positive mental health and have excellent verbal communication and listening skills.
