item.title: Video Production Executive
item.description: About The Role Every story matters here. Some are quiet, some joyful, some hard to tell. As a Video Production Executive at Alzheimer’s Society, you will help bring these stories to life with care, honesty and craft. You will join a creative team that believes in storytelling as a force for understanding, challenge and change. Working with the Video Production Manager, you will create and edit content across social media, interviews, campaign films and longer-form storytelling. This role has a strong focus on editing and post-production. We’re looking for someone who enjoys shaping stories in the edit: finding the right moments, building pace and structure, working with sound and graphics, and turning raw footage into engaging, polished content. People come to this role from many paths, whether film or media training, freelance work, community storytelling or self-taught practice. What matters most is strong editing ability, a good instinct for storytelling and a commitment to creating inclusive, respectful work. What you’ll do You will work across the production process, but a significant part of your role will be focused on editing and post-production, supporting everything from quick-turnaround social content to interviews, campaign films and longer, story-led pieces. Using Adobe Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve or similar professional editing software, alongside tools such as After Effects where appropriate, you will edit raw footage into clear and engaging stories. You will make confident decisions around narrative, pacing, music, sound and visual treatment, as well as adapting content for different channels and formats. You will create cutdowns and different versions of content, add subtitles and graphics, and apply accessibility best practice so our work can reach as many people as possible. You will also have opportunities to support filming and production. This may include shooting interviews and documentary-style content, setting up lighting and sound, and helping to create a calm, respectful environment where people feel comfortable sharing their experiences. Alongside editing and filming, you will support production planning and logistics, including call sheets, scheduling and risk assessments, and contribute creative ideas about how our stories can be brought to life. Collaboration is central. You will work closely with the Video Production Manager and colleagues across our creative and wider teams, respond constructively to feedback and help ensure finished content is delivered accurately and consistently across platforms including social media, YouTube and internal channels. About you We welcome applicants from all backgrounds. You do not need to meet every requirement, and we encourage you to apply if you bring relevant skills and a willingness to learn. You may have: - Experience working across the full video production process, from pre-production through to filming and editing - Strong working knowledge of Adobe Premiere Pro (and ideally After Effects), with the ability to edit content to a high standard - Practical experience recording sound and working with lighting in documentary or factual filming environments - Experience working on story-led content, including supporting people to share personal or sensitive experiences in a respectful and ethical way - An understanding of motion graphics, or a willingness to learn and develop skills in this area - A collaborative and inclusive working style, with strong organisation skills and a commitment to accessible, high-quality storytelling Interviews are provisionally scheduled to take place on the 23rd September via MS Teams About Alzheimer's Society Dementia is the UK's biggest killer. One in three people born in the UK today will develop dementia in their lifetime. At Alzheimer's Society, we're the UK's leading dementia charity and the only one to tackle all aspects of dementia by giving help and hope to people living with dementia today and in the future. We give vital support to people facing the most frightening times of their lives, while also funding groundbreaking research and campaigning to make dementia the priority it should be. Together with our supporters, we're working towards a world where dementia no longer devastates lives. Our values make sure that our focus is clear for the challenges and opportunities ahead and remind us of what we all stand for. Our commitment to Equity, Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging We need to ensure the voices around our table better reflect and understand the communities we exist to serve. We strongly encourage individuals to apply who have a disability, impairment or health condition or individuals who identify as Black, Asian or from another minority ethnic background, as these groups are currently under-represented at Alzheimer's Society. item.title: Junior Designer
item.description: About The Role There’s a moment, just before something goes out into the world, when everything clicks into place. The message is clear, the design feels right, and you know it’s going to connect with someone who needs it. At Alzheimer’s Society, those moments matter. Every piece of creative work helps people affected by dementia feel seen, supported and understood. As a Junior Designer, you’ll play a part in making that happen. Working within our Creative team, you’ll help turn ideas into thoughtful, well-crafted design across digital and print. From campaign visuals to everyday assets, your work will help bring our brand to life in a way that is consistent, accessible and meaningful. You’ll collaborate with designers, content specialists and digital colleagues, learning as you go and building your skills in a supportive, fast-paced environment where your work has real impact. What you’ll do In this role, you’ll spend your time bringing ideas to life through thoughtful, well-crafted design. You’ll work across a mix of digital and print, creating and adapting assets that help communicate important messages and support impactful campaigns. You’ll take creative concepts and shape them into clear, engaging visuals that feel consistent, on brand and accessible to a wide range of audiences. Whether you’re refining layouts, resizing assets or preparing files for delivery, you’ll care about getting the details right. Working closely with colleagues across creative, content and digital teams, you’ll help make sure design supports the bigger picture. You’ll be part of conversations, contribute ideas and collaborate to deliver work that lands well and makes a difference. Alongside this, you’ll manage your own workload, keeping projects moving and maintaining quality even when things are busy. At a glance, you will: - Create and adapt design across digital and print, from social content to campaign materials - Prepare and deliver artwork that meets brand, accessibility and quality standards - Collaborate with colleagues to ensure creative supports wider campaigns and activity - Manage multiple projects and deadlines, staying organised and focused About you You’re someone who cares about the details, but also understands how they fit into the bigger picture. You’re motivated, organised and ready to grow, with a natural ability to keep things moving even when things get busy. You’ll likely bring: - A strong eye for detail and pride in producing accurate, high-quality work - Good project and time management skills, with the ability to prioritise and meet deadlines - Confidence managing more than one task at a time, and knowing how to refocus when priorities shift - A proactive, self-starting approach, taking ownership of your work while knowing when to ask for support - The ability to build positive working relationships with a range of people - Confidence explaining creative ideas in a clear and accessible way, especially to non-design colleagues You care about inclusive design and understand that how something looks is only part of the story. You think about how it’s experienced, making sure your work is clear, accessible and relevant to different audiences, including people affected by dementia. We know that great candidates don’t always meet every requirement. If this role interests you and you feel you could make a difference, we’d love to hear from you. Interviews are provisionally scheduled to take place on the 23rd September via MS Teams. About Alzheimer's Society Dementia is the UK's biggest killer. One in three people born in the UK today will develop dementia in their lifetime. At Alzheimer's Society, we're the UK's leading dementia charity and the only one to tackle all aspects of dementia by giving help and hope to people living with dementia today and in the future. We give vital support to people facing the most frightening times of their lives, while also funding groundbreaking research and campaigning to make dementia the priority it should be. Together with our supporters, we're working towards a world where dementia no longer devastates lives. Our values make sure that our focus is clear for the challenges and opportunities ahead and remind us of what we all stand for. item.title: Venue and Commercial Manager
item.description: Lead our landmark Engine Shed venue and shape unforgettable experiences at the heart of student life. Bring creativity, commercial drive, and operational excellence to one of Northampton’s most iconic spaces. Northampton Students’ Union is searching for an exceptional Venue & Commercial Manager to take the reins of The Engine Shed—our beautifully restored Grade II listed railway building and the beating heart of Waterside Campus. This is a rare opportunity to lead a venue that blends historic character with modern capability, delivering vibrant student events, standout commercial functions, and unforgettable experiences for our community. By day, The Engine Shed is a welcoming social hub where students meet, collaborate, and create memories. By night—and throughout the year—it transforms into a distinctive destination for live events, corporate functions, weddings, conferences, and community celebrations. We’re looking for someone who can harness this potential, driving both operational excellence and commercial growth while championing inclusivity, sustainability, and outstanding service. As Venue & Commercial Manager, you will lead the operational, creative, and commercial development of the venue. You’ll oversee daily operations across the Bar & Café, conferencing, and events, ensuring every aspect of the venue is safe, compliant, welcoming, and running at peak performance. You’ll line‑manage a diverse team—including the Deputy Venue Manager, Caterer, casual staff, and security—creating a positive, collaborative culture where staff thrive and students feel supported. You’ll be the driving force behind our events programme, coordinating everything from student socials to corporate conferences and weddings. You’ll work closely with clients to understand their vision, delivering bespoke, high‑quality experiences that set The Engine Shed apart. You’ll also lead on developing new income streams, crafting business plans, and presenting performance reports to the Commercial Strategy Meeting. Commercial acumen is key. You’ll manage budgets, monitor financial performance, refine pricing strategies, and ensure strong cost control. You’ll also oversee stock management, purchasing, and cash handling, ensuring compliance with SU financial procedures. Your ability to interpret data—tracking conversion metrics from web clicks to confirmed bookings—will help maximise the venue’s commercial potential. Collaboration is central to this role. You’ll work with the Marketing & Communications team to deliver compelling campaigns, build relationships with local businesses and community partners, and champion The Engine Shed’s sustainability credentials. You’ll also work closely with University Estates, Campus Services, elected officers, and SU leadership to ensure the venue continues to evolve in line with student needs and organisational strategy. As the designated Premises Supervisor, you’ll ensure full compliance with the Licensing Act 2003, conduct regular risk assessments, and lead staff training on health and safety and emergency protocols. If you’re an experienced venue operator with creativity, commercial instinct, and a passion for delivering exceptional experiences, we’d love to hear from you. Join us and help shape the next chapter of The Engine Shed—where community, innovation, and unforgettable moments come together.
item.dc:creator: Northampton Students' Union

item.title: Inclusion and Diversity Manager
item.description: Inclusion and Diversity Manager House of Lords – Inclusion and Diversity Team, Human Resources BELONG HERE. TOGETHER, WE MAKE PARLIAMENT HAPPEN. As an Inclusion and Diversity Manager in the House of Lords, you’ll play an important role in supporting the UK’s parliamentary democracy. Your work will help Members and colleagues carry out their responsibilities effectively — contributing to something bigger than any one role. You’ll be part of a collaborative community, working alongside colleagues from a wide range of professions. Together, we make Parliament happen. You’ll be based on the Parliamentary Estate in Westminster — a unique working environment shaped by history and powered by the people who work here today. What you’ll be doing In this role, you’ll: Contribute to a dynamic, high-performing Inclusion and Diversity team that supports the Administration’s value of inclusivity and executes initiatives that deliver on organisational inclusion priorities. Support a range of internal networks and programmes to champion diverse voices in the House of Lords and contribute to a positive workplace culture. Advise and guide colleagues to access the support they need to thrive in the workplace. Work with other functions in HR to draft guidance and policies that support an inclusive working environment and encourages inclusive leadership. What we’re looking for We’re looking for someone who can bring their skills and experience to make a meaningful contribution here. You’ll have: An interest in the House of Lords – Demonstrable interest in and commitment to the role of the House of Lords in parliamentary democracy. Experience with inclusion and diversity – Specialist knowledge and experience working in an inclusion and diversity function, including experience delivering measurable improvements through inclusion and diversity initiatives. Proficiency in strategic working – Experience contributing to and executing initiatives related to strategic objectives. The ability to assess the effectiveness of initiatives and adapt them to meet strategic aims. Competency in project management – Demonstrable ability to independently manage projects and programmes, including their design, delivery, and review to quality, time and budget, alongside “business as usual” and reactive work. It would be even better if you have (or are willing to learn) the: Stakeholder management skills – Proven ability to build effective working relationships with a wider range of stakeholders, including team members, senior leaders, and colleagues from different backgrounds. Ability to problem solve – High level of initiative and adaptability, including the ability to pick up work on short notice, offering resolutions and advice on inclusion and diversity-related issues. Ability to act with professionalism, tact and discretion – Demonstrable competence in managing sensitive issues tactfully and in alignment with the House of Lords Impartiality Guidance, representing the team with professionalism. For full details, please see the job description. What you’ll get in return Working at the House of Lords means joining a community that values your wellbeing, growth and contribution. You’ll benefit from: 30 days annual leave (rising to 35 after one year) Generous Civil Service pension scheme A comprehensive Parliamentary health and wellbeing programme Access to a wide range of learning and development opportunities across diverse professions The chance to witness democracy in action and work in a place of historic national significance The work we do is vital to the House of Lords — the second chamber of the UK Parliament. It plays a critical role in making laws, scrutinising government, and providing independent expertise on national issues. Ready to apply? If you’re looking for an employer where you can belong, grow and thrive, we’d love to hear from you. Please complete your online application by 23:59 on 8 September 2026. We recommend that your application answers do not exceed 300 words.

item.title: COMMUNITY PROJECTS WORKER (OASIS NORTH BRISTOL)
item.description: COMMUNITY PROJECTS WORKER OASIS NORTH BRISTOL HOURS: 8 HOURS PER WEEK (0.2FTE) CONTRACT: 12 MONTH FIXED TERM CONTRACT (Extension dependent on funding) SALARY: £5,673.80 per annum (FTE £28,369 pa for 1FTE) Want to develop, coordinate and manage a food insecurity and community cohesion project offering a diverse range of activities and support for the local community? Want to enable families and local residents to thrive? Want to lead a dynamic, passionate and impactful team of volunteers? Oasis’ vision is for community, a place where everyone is included, making a contribution and reaching their God-given potential. We have an exciting opportunity for a Community Projects Worker to join Oasis North Bristol. Our Community Projects Worker will work with families and residents across the community to develop positive activities and services which promote a sense of belonging and help break the cycle of disadvantage. We’re looking for an individual who has a passion for supporting families and adults, and developing community led activities. The role will involve supporting families and adults in the community, but also families in our local Oasis academies, inspiring and enabling local people to be an active voice and developer in their local area. Key responsibilities include: · To work with the Youth & Community Lead and other team members/partners as required to create and implement a strategy and vision for our food insecurity work. · Ensuring effective financial management and income generation to sustain and expand services · Managing and growing a team of volunteers, ensuring alignment with Oasis’ ethos and values. · Building strong partnerships with local stakeholders to support the delivery of impactful community projects. · Work directly with families and the wider community in a non-judgemental way empowering them and their families to get the most out of the opportunities available. · Create opportunities for families and the community to get involved in shaping and delivering the work of the community projects. · Developing and maintaining monitoring and evaluation frameworks to demonstrate the impact of activities. · Ensure compliance with health and safety, safeguarding, and other statutory requirements. The successful post holder must have: · Excellent organisational and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build positive working relationships. · Good standard of basic education, including English and Maths Level 2 · Proven experience of community work as a volunteer or professionally · Experience of managing and working with volunteers · Ability to build long lasting, positive relationships with both young people and adults · A commitment to the Oasis ethos and values, including inclusion, equality, and perseverance. This is an exciting opportunity to be part of a growing national organisation, making a real difference to communities on a local level. As part of the package, Oasis offers: As part of the package, Oasis offers: · A pension scheme, offering 7% employer contribution. · A generous holiday allowance, starting at 25 days per year (plus 8 Bank Holidays). · Policies which promote well-being and are family friendly. To apply, please send your CV and a Supporting Statement (no more than two A4 pages). Please expand on your CV to tell us about relevant skills, experience and qualification you have, that relate to the job description and person specification. Completed applications should be returned by 9am Wednesday 23rd September 2026. Interviews will take place Thursday 1st October 2026 . W e actively encourage applications from people of all ethnic backgrounds and underrepresented groups. If you require any assistance to overcome potential barriers during the recruitment process, please let us know. We appreciate you may wish to use AI to support elements of your application but we strongly encourage all candidates to submit applications that genuinely reflect their own skills, achievements and lived experiences. It's what makes your application stand out! Oasis is committed to making a difference to the lives of the communities it works in, and as such you must show a willingness to demonstrate commitment to the values and behaviours which flow from the Oasis ethos. We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. We expect all staff to share this commitment and to undergo appropriate checks, including enhanced DBS checks. The successful candidates must have the right to work in the UK. Oasis cannot assist with sponsorship or visas. Oasis supports Equal Opportunities. Registered Charity No. 1163889

item.title: Campaigner - Rapid Response (FTC)
item.description: Amnesty International UK (AIUK) has a simple aim: an end to human rights abuses. Independent, international and influential, we campaign for justice, fairness, freedom and truth wherever they are denied. If you want to use your skills, knowledge, and experience to help fight for human rights, you could be our new Campaigner - Rapid Response. About the role At AIUK, the Campaigns and Political Relations team helps us achieve our goal of bringing an end to human rights abuses by working alongside individuals and communities to build a sustained movement to defend and promote human rights both in the UK and globally. The Campaigner - Rapid Response is accountable for running and assisting on projects and campaigns within our Human Rights Crises programme, focusing on areas including armed conflict, protecting multilateral and international justice mechanisms and other foreign affairs issues. Working with the Campaign Manager they will oversee discreet projects and initiatives as well as playing a key supporting role in the development and delivery of this work, including engaging parliamentarians and organising in key local areas to support localised campaigns. Occasional travel to London will be required for in-person meetings. More details can be found by downloading the job description from our careers portal. The role may be for you if: You're organised and skilled in project management to deliver campaign activities, such as events, communications outputs or local organising and have knowledge of how to bring about change. You are a good communicator and can build effective relationships. You collaborate and positively contribute to an inclusive culture. You can write, edit and develop compelling materials. You also have a good knowledge of UK foreign affairs and political processes. Our Commitment to you Inclusion, Diversity, Equity, and Anti-Racism (IDEA) are at the core of our values. We want to be an organisation that tackles structural inequality and prejudice as well as be an actively anti-racist organisation. This means taking a meaningful and equitable approach to supporting and developing you and others during your time with us. New colleagues receive 27 days leave annually (29 after five years), as well as bank holidays (pro rated for part time) and 3 wellbeing days. 2-5% employee pension contributions are matched at 6-9% and we offer 6 months full pay for family leave. We offer flexible working such as compressed work patterns and job shares. Apply for this role This vacancy advert may be taken down from job boards earlier than the stated deadline if a high standard of applications is received (if you have started an application in our portal, you will still have opportunity to complete it by the original deadline). We welcome applications from everyone and particularly encourage applications from people from an ethnic minority background, and people with a disability to help us achieve a balanced representation in our workforce, especially at senior grades. To reduce bias in our shortlisting process, AIUK operates an anonymised application process. If for any reason you prefer to apply in a different format, or require adjustments in the process, please get in touch. To support all candidates to perform their best at interview, we send interview questions in advance. We are a disability confident organisation. Visit our jobs page for application guidance and information on benefits, recruitment inclusion and hybrid working.

item.title: Rehoming Centre Manager
item.description: Rehoming Centre Manager Beagle Welfare is looking for an experienced, compassionate and highly organised Rehoming Centre Manager to lead the daily operation of our Rehoming Centre, based in Burton-on-Trent. This is a rewarding opportunity to make a visible difference to the lives of beagles, adopters, volunteers and colleagues by creating a centre where excellent welfare, effective rehabilitation and successful rehoming are at the heart of everything we do. As the lead on site, you will manage and develop staff and volunteers, oversee safe and efficient centre operations, and help ensure every beagle in our care receives the right support to progress towards a happy, secure future. You will also represent Beagle Welfare externally and contribute to the continued development of our rehoming work across the UK. About the role You will be responsible for the leadership, performance and smooth running of the Rehoming Centre, including staff and volunteer management, health and safety, site maintenance and the implementation of operational procedures. With rehoming at the centre of your decision-making, you will use data, strong people leadership and sound operational judgement to help improve outcomes for beagles and the people who care for and adopt them. Key responsibilities · Lead, motivate and develop a committed team of staff and volunteers, creating a positive, inclusive and high-performing culture. · Oversee day-to-day centre operations, ensuring high standards of dog welfare, customer service, health and safety, security and compliance. · Drive rehoming activity by supporting case progression, promoting beagles effectively and helping minimise the time beagles spend in our care. · Manage resources, reporting and administrative processes accurately and responsibly. · Build productive relationships with adopters, visitors, animal welfare organisations, and community partners. · Use data, feedback and quality assurance processes to identify improvements and support consistent application of procedures. About you We are looking for a confident manager with experience leading diverse teams, delivering against targets and managing a varied operational workload. You will be comfortable working around dogs, including beagles with different welfare and behavioural needs, and able to balance compassion with practical decision-making. Strong communication, organisation, collaboration and stakeholder management skills are essential, as is experience in supporting continuous improvement. You will also need a UK manual driving licence and be comfortable driving our van. Experience in a kennel or animal welfare environment would be advantageous, but above all you will share Beagle Welfare’s commitment to improving the lives of beagles and supporting the people who care for them. Working pattern and location This role is based at the Rehoming Centre and offers employment that includes employer provided accommodation (3-bedroom cottage) as part of the compensation package. The centre operates between 08:30 and 17:00 every day of the year, so weekend and bank holiday working will be required on a rota basis. Why join Beagle Welfare? You will join an organisation driven by purpose, teamwork and a shared commitment to dog welfare. This is a hands-on leadership role where your decisions, energy and care will directly support better outcomes for beagles, adopters, volunteers and colleagues.

item.title: Senior Campaign Manager (Trusts and Foundations)
item.description: Prospectus is delighted to be supporting a London health charity in the search for a new Senior Campaign Manager (Trusts and Foundations) to join their dynamic fundraising department. This charity supports the 17,000 staff and 2 million patients of the Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust, across Barnet, Chase Farm, North Mid and Royal Free hospitals, plus over 30 NHS services. The Royal Free Charity is now preparing for an ambitious £50million fundraising campaign in support of a ground-breaking £100million cancer centre. As the Senior Campaign Manager, you will lead on developing and implementing a comprehensive Trusts & Foundations strategy to secure six- and seven-figure gifts in support of the Join the Future Capital Campaign for the new Cancer Centre. This role will identify, cultivate, and steward relationships with Trusts and Foundations to secure income in line with campaign targets. With the support of the wider philanthropy team, the Head of Philanthropy and Campaign, as well as support from a Prospect Research team, this role will be a pivotal role in the campaign's success. To be successful within this Senior Campaign Manager role, you will have proven experience of securing income from trusts and foundations. You will have examples of securing six- or seven-figure gifts, and ideally have capital campaign knowledge and experience. Collaborating with various stakeholders internally and externally, this person will also be a good communicator and able to build strong long-term relationships. At Prospectus, we invest in your journey as a candidate and are committed to supporting you with your application. We welcome all candidates to apply, regardless of age, sex/gender, disability, race, religion, sexual orientation, marital status or pregnancy/maternity. If you have any disability and require reasonable adjustment/s to any part of the process then please contact Rhiannon Mehta at Prospectus. In order to apply, please submit an up-to-date CV and cover letter (max 2 pages) in the first instance. Should your experience be suitable, we will arrange for a meeting to brief you on the role. item.title: Community Fundraising Executive
item.description: Join a respected charity at a pivotal time and help grow vital community income across the North Midlands and Scotland. This is a hands-on role for a motivated fundraiser who enjoys building relationships, delivering events, and providing outstanding supporter care. Working on a hybrid basis with two days per week in Sheffield, you’ll play a key part in connecting local communities with a cause that makes a tangible difference. About the Role: You will lead and coordinate community fundraising activity across the North Midlands and Scotland, driving income through events, challenges and supporter-led initiatives. Working closely with local supporters, groups and partners, you will ensure every interaction is well-managed, recorded and maximised for long-term engagement. This temporary role will have a direct impact on the charity’s ability to fund services and reach more people in need. Key Responsibilities: * Plan, deliver and evaluate a calendar of community fundraising events and activities across the North Midlands and Scotland. * Support, steward and motivate individual fundraisers, community groups and corporate supporters to maximise their fundraising potential. * Manage and update the CRM and donor database to ensure accurate recording of supporter interactions, income and event activity. * Coordinate logistics for community events, including venues, materials, volunteer support and risk assessments. * Develop tailored fundraising materials and communications to engage and retain community supporters. * Provide timely, high-quality supporter care, responding to enquiries and ensuring a positive experience at every touchpoint. * Monitor income and activity performance, producing regular reports and insights to inform future planning. * Collaborate with internal teams to align community fundraising with wider campaigns and brand messaging. Key Requirements: * Proven experience in community fundraising or a closely related fundraising role. * Demonstrable track record in planning, managing and delivering fundraising events and activities. * Strong CRM and donor database management skills, with experience of maintaining accurate records and generating reports. * Excellent relationship-building skills, with the ability to engage and motivate a wide range of supporters. * Strong organisational and time-management abilities, capable of managing multiple projects across a wide geographic area. * High standard of written and verbal communication, with confident presentation skills. * Ability to work on a hybrid basis with two days per week in Sheffield and travel across the North Midlands and Scotland as required. * Comfortable working to income targets and deadlines in a fast-paced environment. Desirable Skills: * Experience working within a charity or non-profit fundraising team. * Familiarity with fundraising regulations and best practice in supporter care. * Experience of virtual or hybrid fundraising events and digital engagement. * Knowledge of the North Midlands and Scotland fundraising landscape and local networks. * Competence in using email marketing tools or basic design software to create supporter communications. Qualifications: * Educated to degree level or equivalent experience in fundraising, marketing, events or a related field. * Formal fundraising training or certification (e.g. Institute of Fundraising) preferred. * Evidence of ongoing professional development in fundraising, events or supporter engagement. If you are a proactive community fundraiser ready to make an immediate impact in a temporary role, we’d welcome your application. Join us and help strengthen community support across the North Midlands and Scotland. essential criteria on the person specification and clearly provide as much information as possible with examples to demonstrate how and where you meet the criteria.

item.title: Fundraising Manager
item.description: Reports to : Chief Executive Officer, working closely with the Programmes Lead and Finance & Governance Lead. Hours : We anticipate appointing this role as a 2 days per week (0.4 FTE) employee. However, we are also open to hearing from experienced freelance fundraising professionals who are interested in delivering an agreed programme of work on a consultancy basis, equivalent to approximately one day per week. Salary : Employee: £27,000–£31,000 FTE (£10,800–£12,400 pro rata for 2 days/16 hours per week), depending on experience. Consultancy: Day rate to be agreed, depending on experience and scope of work. Location : Remote, with approximately two consecutive days per month at our office in Liverpool and occasional travel for meetings or events. Contract: 24 month fixed term (with the intention to extend, subject to funding). Probation Period: 3 months Line Management: This role has no line management responsibility. About Worldwide Radiology Worldwide Radiology is a UK registered charity working to improve access to high-quality diagnostic imaging in low- and middle-income countries. Working alongside hospitals, universities and health partners around the world, we develop practical, sustainable solutions that strengthen radiology services and improve patient care. Much of our work is delivered through a global network of volunteers and long-term partnerships. We're at an exciting stage in our development. Over recent years our fundraising income has grown significantly, but we're now looking to broaden and strengthen our funding base so we can increase our impact. This new role offers the opportunity to become Worldwide Radiology's dedicated fundraising lead, helping shape the next stage of the organisation's growth. About the Role This is an excellent opportunity for an ambitious fundraiser ready to take the next step in their career and take ownership of fundraising within a growing charity. As Worldwide Radiology's dedicated fundraising professional, you will lead our day-to-day fundraising activity across community fundraising, individual giving and trusts and foundations. You'll be responsible for planning and delivering fundraising campaigns, stewarding donors and writing funding applications that help sustain and grow our work. You'll also support the CEO and Programmes Lead in developing larger strategic partnerships with major funders and corporate partners through research, proposal coordination and pipeline management. Unlike many early-career fundraising roles, this position offers genuine ownership from early on. You'll lead fundraising across your portfolio while working closely with colleagues who have experience securing grants and developing partnerships, giving you the support and mentoring to develop your skills and confidence. While we expect to appoint a Fundraising Manager on a part-time basis, we also recognise that an experienced fundraising consultant may bring a different but equally valuable skillset. We're therefore open to considering either model, provided the successful candidate can take ownership of our fundraising programme and help build the systems, relationships and pipeline needed to support Worldwide Radiology's long-term growth. What Success Looks Like During your first 12–18 months you will: Lead successful delivery of WWR's community fundraising programme, including the Big Give Christmas Challenge and other supporter campaigns. Develop and manage a healthy pipeline of trust and foundation applications. Build strong relationships with our existing donors and funders. Help diversify the organisation's income by developing new fundraising opportunities. Introduce systems and processes that strengthen fundraising as the organisation continues to grow. Key Responsibilities Fundraising (Lead) You will take ownership of WWR's fundraising activity across your portfolio, working closely with the CEO while leading delivery day-to-day. Responsibilities include: Leading delivery of fundraising across community fundraising, individual giving and smaller trusts and foundations. Researching, writing and submitting grant applications to trusts and foundations. Managing relationships with existing trust funders and individual donors, including stewardship and reporting. Planning and delivering community fundraising campaigns, supporter events and online fundraising activities, including the Big Give Christmas Challenge and JustGiving campaigns. Developing opportunities to grow our supporter base and increase donor retention. Maintaining accurate fundraising records, donor data and reporting. Monitoring fundraising activity and providing regular updates to the CEO. Supporting the development of fundraising plans and identifying new income opportunities. Partnerships (Support) Working alongside the CEO and Programmes Lead, you will: Research prospective major trusts, foundations and corporate partners. Prepare briefing papers and background research ahead of meetings. Coordinate development of larger funding proposals by gathering information, managing timelines and tracking actions. Maintain the strategic funding pipeline and prospect tracker. Support follow-up from meetings, conferences and partnership discussions. Help identify opportunities to strengthen relationships with healthcare organisations, companies and strategic partners. Person Specification We recognise that no candidate will meet every criterion. If you can demonstrate most of the following, we'd love to hear from you: Experience in a fundraising, development or partnerships role within the charity sector. Experience researching and writing, or supporting the development of, funding applications to trusts and foundations. Excellent written communication skills with the ability to write compelling funding applications and supporter communications. Excellent relationship-building skills, with experience working positively with supporters, volunteers, partners or external stakeholders. Strong organisational skills, with the ability to maintain accurate records and manage information across multiple projects and deadlines. Comfortable working in a digital, remote environment and confident learning new systems, including fundraising CRM platforms. Enthusiasm for Worldwide Radiology's mission and the role of global health partnerships. Desirable attributes: Experience delivering community fundraising campaigns or challenge events. Experience using fundraising CRMs or donor databases. Experience of the Big Give Christmas Challenge or similar match-funding campaigns. Experience supporting corporate partnerships or major donor fundraising. An interest in global health, healthcare or international development. Why Join Worldwide Radiology? This is a rare opportunity to take ownership of fundraising within a growing international charity at an early stage in your career. You'll have the chance to lead fundraising campaigns, develop relationships with donors and funders, and shape how fundraising grows over the coming years. At the same time, you'll benefit from the guidance and support of experienced colleagues, giving you the opportunity to develop your skills while making a tangible contribution to improving access to diagnostic imaging around the world. We're committed to supporting your professional development through mentoring, networking opportunities and relevant fundraising training, helping you build the skills and experience to progress your fundraising career. We offer: Flexible remote working. A collaborative, supportive team with minimal hierarchy. Opportunities for professional development and responsibility. Up to 4% matched pension contribution. 25 days Annual leave plus 8 public holidays (pro rata).

item.title: Marketing Manager Brand
item.description: About The Role What if a brand marketing campaign could make more people aware that dementia is the UK’s biggest killer? Encourage someone caring for a loved one with dementia to seek support? Or inspire more people to use their voice and help make dementia a public priority? That’s the kind of difference your work could make as Marketing Manager (Brand) at Alzheimer’s Society. You’ll join our Brand Marketing team at an exciting time. Following the success of campaigns including The Ultimate Vow, The Long Goodbye and, currently, A Personal Appeal, we’re on a mission to grow the public’s awareness of dementia and Alzheimer’s Society’s unique role in tackling the devastation of this disease. You’ll work alongside the Senior Marketing Manager (Brand) to deliver the next advert in the A Personal Appeal series, develop strategic, innovative brand activations and partnerships and help shape where our brand goes next. Do you have experience of turning an insight into a powerful idea that people can’t forget? Or working with a variety of stakeholders to create work that reaches the right people in the right places to inspire action? In this role, you’ll help us do exactly that. Contract: This is a fixed-term contract until October 2027 Interviews: Interviews are provisionally scheduled to take place on the 16th September via MS Teams What you'll do You’ll help develop brand campaigns, activations and partnerships from an initial idea through to testing, creative execution and delivery across a range of channels. And you’ll work collaboratively throughout the process with both our trusted creative and media planning agencies and internal stakeholders to build sector-leading work. You’ll: - Lead and project manage the delivery of large-scale, multi-channel brand marketing campaigns, keeping projects on track and working to agreed deadlines and budgets. - Develop and deliver paid media strategies across AV, digital, out of home and print channels. - Work closely with our creative and media agencies, building positive relationships and creating the conditions for brilliant work that makes people sit up and take notice. - Drill down into audience insights, research and campaign performance to understand what’s working and where we can shift our approach to achieve organisational objectives. - Bring colleagues and stakeholders with you along the way, so people across the organisation understand and feel connected to our campaigns. - Help shape our brand strategy and make sure everything we produce feels consistent, relevant and inclusive. - Manage significant budgets, making thoughtful decisions about where our investment can have the greatest impact. - Consult on the strategic and creative development of key fundraising products, finding opportunities to connect our brand and fundraising activity.Line manage and support the Senior Marketing Executive (Brand), helping them develop and grow in their role. - Deputise for the Senior Marketing Manager (Brand) when needed. Some days will involve big ideas and inspiring creative conversations. Others will be about budgets, timelines, analysing data and getting the small details just right. You’ll need to be comfortable with both sides of this coin, while keeping sight of why this work matters to our audiences. About you You’ll be a confident and thoughtful marketer who understands what makes a strong brand - and how good marketing can help an organisation connect with more people and achieve its goals. You might have developed your skills in a charity, agency, commercial organisation or somewhere completely different. What matters is what you can bring to the role, the way you work with others and your motivation to create work that truly makes a difference. We’re looking for someone who can: - Lead and project manage large-scale, successful, multi-channel campaigns, balancing competing priorities and keeping delivery on track to tight deadlines. - Develop and deliver multi-channel paid media strategies, using insights and performance data to make informed decisions. - Manage, track and make effective use of significant budgets, with a clear focus on value and impact. - Work collaboratively with creative and media agencies, providing clear direction, challenging constructively and creating space for ideas to bloom. - Communicate clearly, build trusted relationships and influence a broad range of stakeholders, including senior colleagues. - Understand how brand marketing can build trust, awareness and engagement to support a charity’s wider goals. - Use research, data and insights to understand what matters to people, translating learnings into compelling brand campaigns and partnerships. You’ll be comfortable bringing both creative flair and analytical thinking to your work. You’ll be organised, curious and able to manage your own workload, while also knowing when to involve others or ask for support. Most importantly, you’ll care deeply about the work you produce and the people it’s reaching. We value different perspectives, backgrounds and ways of thinking, and we know there are many different routes into a role like this. If you can see yourself doing this role but don’t meet every single requirement, please don’t let that stop you from applying. We’d love to hear from you. About Alzheimer's Society Dementia is the UK's biggest killer. One in three people born in the UK today will develop dementia in their lifetime. At Alzheimer's Society, we're the UK's leading dementia charity and the only one to tackle all aspects of dementia by giving help and hope to people living with dementia today and in the future. We give vital support to people facing the most frightening times of their lives, while also funding groundbreaking research and campaigning to make dementia the priority it should be. Together with our supporters, we're working towards a world where dementia no longer devastates lives. Our values make sure that our focus is clear for the challenges and opportunities ahead and remind us of what we all stand for. Our commitment to Equity, Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging We need to ensure the voices around our table better reflect and understand the communities we exist to serve. We strongly encourage individuals to apply who have a disability, impairment or health condition or individuals who identify as Black, Asian or from another minority ethnic background, as these groups are currently under-represented at Alzheimer's Society. We want everyone we work with, as a colleague, volunteer, supporter, or someone we support, to feel included and that they belong at Alzheimer's Society. Our Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Strategy here along with our internal employee forum and Employee Lived Experience network groups help us promote inclusion and belonging, becoming an engaged and inclusive organisation for all our people. Our hiring process During your recruitment process we want to make sure that you bring your whole self and can be at your best. We are working hard to ensure our recruitment process is as inclusive as possible, so please do inform us of your experience and anything you think we could do better by completing our candidate survey when you apply. Please also contact Alzheimer's Society Talent Acquisition Team via [email protected] for application support or any adjustments you might need. To ensure fairness and consistency to select the best candidate for this role, all our applications are anonymised up until an interview has been confirmed. We recognise the benefits of AI, but if you're considering using it to submit your application, we encourage you to reflect on the value it truly adds. AI tools often lack the personal touch and authenticity that set candidates apart. We want to hear your unique perspective, experiences, and skills, so we encourage you to showcase them in your own voice. We try to avoid closing roles early where possible, however if we receive a high volume of applications, we may close earlier than the advertised closing date. Should this occur, we will aim to provide you with at least 48 hours' notice. We are committed to safer recruitment and ensuring the welfare of those we work with, due to the nature of some of our roles, we might need to carry out a Criminal Record Check at the relevant level. You can read more information via our Website. Giving back to you Our employees work hard every day to make a true difference in people's lives. We are proud to support them with a range of benefits, recognition and many options for working agilely, all contributing to a strong work life balance. We also have various learning programmes to support you in your development and help you grow to realise your potential and shape a career with Alzheimer's Society. You can also visit our Working for Us pages, which give you more information about what it's like to be an employee at the Society. INDAZ

item.title: Sporting + Events Senior Officer
item.description: Location: Hybrid working between the Aldgate, London office and home We will be a participating charity in the TCS London Marathon 2027 Double, meaning we’ll have teams on both the Saturday and Sunday of the event weekend. This is an exciting time for an experienced and motivated Sporting + Events Senior Officer to join our Sporting + Events (S+E) Team and help us deliver the London Marathon 2027 and 2028 to an exceptional standard. Asthma + Lung UK is the only charity in the UK fighting for everyone with a lung condition, aiming for a world where everyone can breathe with healthy lungs. We fund cutting-edge research, provide advice and support for the 12 million people who will get a lung condition during their lifetime. We also campaign for clean air and for better NHS diagnosis and treatment. The Sporting + Events team are working on an ambitious portfolio of events and strategy to continue our recent income growth in this area. This will be a crucial role within the team, supporting the S+E Manager with operational decision-making and leading on event logistics. You’ll play a key role in overseeing the overall stewardship programme, supporting the Officer to deliver fantastic supporter care. You’ll closely monitor financial and engagement data to track progress, allowing you to make robust recommendations to the Manager to enhance performance. You’ll also have the opportunity to line manage an Assistant as part of this role offering great experience for those looking to progress to Manager level within the sector. To be successful in this role, you will have an excellent track record of delivering mass participation events, as well as reaching agreed KPIs. You’ll be enthusiastic, organised and ready to join a friendly, ambitious and high-performing team to reach new records. As well as a competitive salary, you’ll enjoy a range of benefits including 30 days (pro rata) annual leave plus bank holidays, membership of a health cash plan, employee assistance programme and pension scheme. This is a fantastic opportunity to join an ambitious team at a pivotal time within in our strategy. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, so we encourage you to submit your application at the earliest opportunity to ensure consideration.

item.title: Outreach Manager
item.description: Location : Remote; able to travel into London easily Beneﬁts : Flexible working, private healthcare, 35 days annual leave (in addition to bank holidays), £500 contribution towards work laptop Reporting to: Director About the Schools Consent Project The Schools Consent Project is a UK-based charity dedicated to educating young people about sexual consent and healthy relationships. We deliver workshops in schools and educational settings led by trained volunteer lawyers. By introducing consent literacy at school, young people are more likely to make informed, ethical decisions and are less likely to experience or perpetrate sexual violence in later life. Through this hire, we aim to scale access to high-quality consent education. Role Summary The Outreach Manager is responsible for driving the expansion of the Schools Consent Project’s reach, engagement, and impact across London and the South East. Acting as the organisation’s lead “sales” and business development professional, you will contribute to and manage our strong pipeline of partner schools and organisations, convert leads into confirmed bookings, and maximise long-term engagement. You will own the end-to-end outreach and partnership journey: from prospecting and lead generation, through relationship development and negotiation, to repeat engagement and retention. Key Responsibilities Business Development & Lead Generation • Develop and execute a proactive outreach and growth strategy to increase workshop bookings. • Develop and maintain relationships with existing schools; ensure SCP’s workshop content remains responsive and reactive to the emerging concerns of young people when it comes to sex, consent and the online world. • Generate leads through cold outreach, referrals, events, and campaigns. • Contribute to and maintain a pipeline of new schools and educational settings. • Reinvigorate historic relationships with schools. Account Management • Convert enquiries and prospects into confirmed programme partners. • Present the charity’s offer and impact to senior school leaders, safeguarding leads, and decision-makers. • Manage key accounts and ensure high levels of partner satisfaction and retention. • Promote additional workshops and programmes where appropriate (eg. teacher training; parent workshops). • Track booking trends eg. seasonal vs. reactive bookings; develop a communication strategy around each ‘type’ of school, involving timely booking reminders. Pipeline, Targets & Performance • Manage outreach targets for bookings, partnerships, and regional coverage. • Monitor conversion rates, pipeline value, and performance metrics. • Produce regular forecasts and performance reports. • Use data and insight to refine sales strategies and improve outcomes. Marketing & Promotion • Help develop compelling outreach materials and campaigns. • Deliver presentations, webinars, and pitches to prospective educational partners. • Represent the organisation at conferences, networks, and sector events. • Help gather case studies, testimonials, and impact data to support outreach and fundraising. Delivery Coordination • Work closely with our Volunteer Manager and Operations Manager to match supply with demand. • Ensure smooth handover from booking to delivery. • Anticipate capacity constraints and manage partner expectations. Team Leadership & Development • Contribute to the development of outreach systems, processes, and tools. • Share insights and learning across the organisation. • Oversee team members currently managing school outreach. Person Specification Essential Criteria • Proven experience in sales, business development, partnerships, or outreach roles. • Experience working with schools, education providers, or youth services. • Track record of meeting or exceeding targets. • Excellent communication skills. • Strong relationship management and account development experience. • Highly organised, with strong CRM and data management skills. • Ability to work autonomously and drive results. Desirable Criteria • Experience working in the charity, education, or public sectors. • Knowledge of safeguarding and child protection frameworks. • Understanding of social impact measurement. Values and Approach We are looking for someone who: • Is committed to our mission and values. • Demonstrates empathy, professionalism, and integrity. • Works collaboratively and inclusively. • Is proactive, adaptable, and solution-focused. Safeguarding and Equality The Schools Consent Project is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. All staff are expected to share this commitment. We are an equal opportunities employer and welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds. We ask applicants to draft their applications without using AI (save for checking spelling or grammar), so that we can get a real sense of your suitability for the role.

item.title: Reporting Analyst
item.description: About The Role At Alzheimer’s Society, data plays an important role in our mission to create a world where dementia no longer devastates lives. Are you ready to turn raw data into insights that drive real change? Do you want to be part of a mission where your data skills directly contribute to improving lives? We’re looking for a Reporting Analyst to play a central role within the Services Data Team, as part of our Technology Directorate, helping teams across the society make evidence-based decisions that truly matter. In this role, you’ll unlock the stories hidden within our data. From operational reports that keep the day-to-day running smoothly, to Commissioner reporting that shapes our future. Using tools like Power BI for data visualisation, SQL for data manipulation, and even advanced techniques with R and GIS, you’ll create clear, user-friendly reports that empower teams to make a difference. Beyond building reports, you’ll be a trusted partner and problem-solver, gathering requirements, defining reporting standards, and delivering training to help colleagues confidently use data to achieve their goals. Join us and help ensure data becomes a powerful tool in the fight against dementia. About you You are passionate about using data to create meaningful change and thrive in a collaborative environment. You enjoy solving complex problems, turning data into actionable insights, and empowering others to use data effectively. - Proven experience designing and delivering Business Intelligence and Management Information reports. - Proficiency in Power BI, SQL scripting, and data manipulation. - The ability to create dashboards and visual reports that are intuitive and actionable. - Experience working collaboratively with stakeholders to gather and interpret requirements. - A strong understanding of data governance and reporting standards. - Excellent problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and a proactive approach to ensuring data accuracy. - Strong communication skills to engage with technical and non-technical audiences alike. Nice-to-haves - Experience with R and GIS (Geographic Information Systems) for advanced analytics and geospatial insights. - Familiarity with Agile development practices and iterative delivery. - Knowledge of working with external suppliers to manage data integration and reporting requirements. What you’ll focus on: - Designing, developing, and maintaining high-quality reports and dashboards using tools like Power BI, SQL, R, and GIS to provide actionable insights. - Collaborating with teams to gather and prioritise reporting requirements, ensuring solutions meet organisational needs and support evidence-based decisions. - Defining and enforcing reporting standards and governance, maintaining consistency and accuracy across datasets. - Using Agile practices to quickly prototype, refine, and deliver impactful reporting solutions. - Supporting data quality by developing integrity scripts and validating reports to ensure accuracy and compliance. - Delivering support and guidance to help colleagues confidently interpret and utilise reports in their work. item.title: Housing Manager
item.description: About the Role A home is more than a property. It’s the foundation for independence, security and belonging. As Housing Manager at Norwood, you’ll provide a high-quality, compliant and person-centred housing management service across a portfolio of our supported living properties. You’ll take ownership of the full tenancy journey, from allocation and sign-up through to tenancy sustainment and move-on. But this role is about much more than managing agreements and processes. You’ll build relationships with the people we support, understand what matters to them and help ensure their homes are safe, well maintained and appropriate to their individual needs. You’ll conduct regular tenancy visits and property inspections, support people to understand their rights and responsibilities, and help resolve issues before they put a tenancy at risk. Working closely with our Property and Operations teams, Registered Managers, families, advocates and external partners, you’ll bring together strong housing practice with an understanding of the individual. Your impact will be clear: sustainable tenancies, safer homes, greater independence and a positive experience for the people who call them home. About Norwood Founded in 1795, Norwood is the oldest Jewish charity in the UK. We support and empower neurodiverse children and their families and people with neurodevelopmental disabilities to live their best lives. At Norwood, you will make a real difference every day. You will be part of a supportive and inclusive team where kindness is shown in how we care, respect shapes how we work together, belonging ensures everyone feels valued, and empowerment enables people to thrive. We invest in your growth, care about your wellbeing, and give you the pride of knowing your work changes lives. Who We Are Looking For You’ll be an experienced housing professional who understands that good housing management starts with the person. You’ll bring strong tenancy management experience and a sound understanding of housing law, regulation and compliance. You’ll be confident managing the practical realities of a housing portfolio, including tenancy agreements, rent accounts, arrears, voids, repairs, inspections, tenancy breaches and disputes. Alongside that technical knowledge, you’ll know how to build trust. You’ll be able to adapt your communication to individual needs, explain sometimes complex housing matters clearly and make sure the people we support understand their tenancy, their rights and the choices available to them. You’ll be comfortable working collaboratively with support teams, families, advocates, social workers, local authorities, housing providers and other partners to resolve issues and achieve positive outcomes. Most importantly, you’ll combine professional judgement with a person-centred approach, recognising that behind every tenancy is someone’s home, independence and sense of security. Your Day to Day You’ll: Take ownership of a defined portfolio of supported living properties and manage the full tenancy lifecycle Conduct regular visits with tenants to review their tenancy, identify emerging issues and support tenancy sustainment Carry out property inspections during scheduled visits, identifying repairs, property condition and health and safety concerns Ensure tenancy agreements, records and documentation remain accurate, up to date and fit for purpose Deliver accessible tenancy sign-ups using approaches appropriate to individual communication needs, including easy-read information and visual aids Help tenants understand their rights, responsibilities and security of tenure Monitor rent accounts and manage arrears proactively Support tenants with Housing Benefit applications and other relevant benefits, including liaison or signposting to specialist agencies where appropriate Manage tenancy breaches, anti-social behaviour and disputes proportionately and with a trauma-informed approach Oversee allocations, voids and move-on arrangements Work with Property Services to make sure repairs and maintenance are addressed promptly Help ensure homes are safe, compliant, well maintained and appropriate for neurodiverse needs, including sensory considerations Build strong relationships with tenants, families and advocates Facilitate tenant engagement and ensure the tenant voice influences how services develop Promote independence, participation and community inclusion Identify and respond appropriately to safeguarding concerns Work collaboratively with social workers, support teams and other professionals Develop relationships with local authorities, housing associations, registered providers, private landlords and benefits agencies Contribute to audits, inspections, reporting and continuous service improvement Qualifications, Training & Experience Essential You’ll bring: A housing qualification or be working towards one Effective tenancy management experience Experience delivering performance measures and improving customer service within a housing management environment Knowledge of exempt accommodation Strong knowledge and understanding of housing legislation and tenancy management Experience working collaboratively to deliver improvements for customers Understanding of the Renters’ Rights Act 2026 Knowledge of safeguarding legislation Understanding of the Equality Act and inclusive practice Knowledge of health and safety compliance An understanding of neurodiversity, including autism, ADHD and learning disabilities Strong communication and interpersonal skills The ability to adapt your communication to individual needs Strong problem-solving and conflict-resolution skills Good organisation and workload management Desirable It would be advantageous if you also bring: Experience within supported housing or social care Knowledge of welfare benefits Experience working directly with neurodiverse people Reward and Benefits 21 days annual leave + 8 Bank Holidays (FTE) + Jewish Festival Days Enhanced parental pay Employee Assistance Programme Health cash plan covering dental, optical, and therapy treatments, with virtual GP access, private consultations, and wellbeing tools via the My Medicash App Blue Light Card scheme access Cycle to Work scheme Free on-site parking A supportive, and experienced leadership team. A bit more information: Norwood’s Broadway House, located at 80 - 82 The Broadway, Stanmore HA7 4HB, is the charity’s head office and main administrative base. It brings together Governance, Leadership, Fundraising, Finance, People and Culture, and Marketing and Communications, providing coordination and support to Children & Family Services and Adult Services. The office supports Norwood’s mission to help people with neurodevelopmental disabilities, their families, and children in need across London and the South East. It is also the main point of contact for referrals, general enquiries, and charity business. item.title: Community Development Worker
item.description: Join a vibrant and brave grassroots organisation led by Gypsy and Traveller people in West Yorkshire. Leeds Gypsy and Traveller Exchange (Leeds GATE) is an established and award-winning civil societyorganisationwith a national profile. We arerecognisedas being innovative, brave and creative.Our overall aim is to improve the quality of life for Gypsies andTravellersthrough addressing inequalities in homes, health, education, and employment, financial and social inclusion. We run a number ofa communityfacing and strategic projects to achieve our aims including advocacy, community development and youth work.Those who access our services and activities are members of Leeds GATE. Job Purpose: Working in Wakefield and Calderdale you will build trusted relationships with Leeds GATE members, residents and families living on the Heath Common local authority site (Wakefield), yards, houses and roadside across the Wakefield district and Calderdale Borough. Through your relationships you will gain understanding of people’s strengths, interests and hobbies, whilst also building up knowledge of the needs of support, barriers and issues faced by Gypsies and Travellers. As a community development worker you will help to develop and create opportunities to engage the community, such as activities and group work, thinking how these can help people to share their ideas, develop their skills, build confidence and empower them, as well as improving health and wellbeing outcomes to enable better lives. An element of hybrid working is supported within this role but it is expected that the majority of work (80%) will be based on sites, outreach and community based events.

item.title: CEO
item.description: Information about Headway Gloucestershire:- Headway Gloucestershire was established in 1987 and since then has been working to make a positive difference to the lives of people over 18 with an acquired brain injury. We provide specialist recovery support and respite through the following services Our Community Links Service provides outreach information, specialist brain injury recoveryadvice for people with an acquired brain injury and their families and supports them as they come toterms with the changed circumstances brought about by brain injury. The service includes benefits advice and collaborative working with other organisations such as Adult Social Services, Housing Providers and other VCSE organisations Our Enablement Service is centre based and open every weekday offering activities that focus on the five elements of rehabilitation: emotional functioning; cognitive functioning; learning; social interaction and behaviour. This takes the form of a structured timetable so that those with an acquired brain injury can select the activities thathelp them work towards their goals.We work one to one and also employ a group format to harness theunique recovery benefits of peer contact and support. Our Carer Support Groups provide a relaxed environment withinthe community where people with an acquired brain injury and their families can meet new people, share experiences and support each other.We provide training events, social events and facilitate familysupport groups. Our Peer Support Groups provide an opportunity once a month in different locations for people with an acquired brain injury to discuss topics of interest and to share challenges, tips and provide positive support. Our Community Hubs are delivered in locations around the county in community venues and are tailored to the needs of the group for up to 3 hours. They include physical exercise sessions, focussed discussion groups, advice and support related to acquired brain injury and the opportunity to develop a local support network Our Hospital Liaison service is where we attend the Gloucester Royal Hospital once every two weeks at an agreed time to offer support to individuals and their family during the early stages of rehabilitation. Headway Gloucestershire is a busy, growing charity providing services to people with an acquired brain injury and their families and carers. Every year we are challenged to raise funds to help deliver our services. CEO Role You will lead and motivate a small team of staff and volunteers and work with them to provide a person centred, enabling and outcome focused support service to people over 18 with an acquired brain injury. You will seek opportunities for planned development and growth and build on the success of our existing services to increase our offer. You will act as principal spokesperson and advocate for the charity, demonstrating integrity and commitment to key stakeholders, partners and donors to ensure the best outcomes for people affected by brain injury in the Gloucestershire area. You will be joining at an exciting time as we work together with health and social care partners to monitor and understand the needs of people with brain injury in Gloucestershire and influence the pathway for rehabilitation and longer-term support. The ideal candidate will have experience of managing a small organisation in the charity or care sector, developing strategy and business plans, a track record of securing funding in a tough financial climate, excellent communication skills and the ability to motivate and develop a team of staff and volunteers. Headway Gloucestershire is an equal opportunity employer and committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and adults at risk. The successful applicant will need to undertake an enhanced DBS check. Salary £50,000 - £52,000 (Pro Rata) with a possible bonus for meeting agreed fundraising targets Based at Headway House, Gloucester Hours 37.5 hours per week with the option of some flexibility depending on business need Contract Permanent Responsible to The Board of Trustees To find out more about this role, please email us. To apply for this position please send your CV and maximum of a two-page personal statement outlining how you meet the requirements for the role.

item.title: Wellbeing Practitioner
item.description: Wellbeing Practitioner Location: Hybrid working, employees work across Office or in probation offices across Wiltshire. The office is in Swindon, England Salary : £26,097 per annum Vacancy Type: Permanent, Full Time (38 hours per week) At Catch22, we are proud of our reputation as a modern and progressive employer. Our 1,300 colleagues and 300 volunteers work at every stage of the social welfare cycle, supporting over 60,000 individuals from cradle to career. In Social Justice, we work with young people and adults in custody and in the community, providing a range of services including offender management and resettlement, mentoring, veterans in custody, victim services, gangs work and youth justice. We believe that with effective support mechanisms and the correct interventions, we can change service user’s ideology, helping them desist from crime and reach their true potential. Job Description This post presents an exciting opportunity to become a Wellbeing Practitioner at our Personal Wellbeing service covering the Wiltshire area. Commissioned by HMPPS this service is focused on supporting adult male ex-offenders by delivering focussed interventions across the following pathways: Family and Significant Others Lifestyle and Associates Emotional Wellbeing Services Social Inclusion Your role will be to support service users to develop strategies to manage emotions and deliver skills training to foster self-confidence by knowing how to access appropriate support. You will also support service users to increase capacity to undertake activities to support daily living and advocate for service users in conjunction with multi-agency partners to engage with treatment and other professionals/services (MH teams/support groups) Your role will support our team in achieving our Justice Business Plan objectives: innovate, revitalise and reform the delivery of Justice Services. Essential Driving license and access to a Vehicle (this role will require travel to offices across the Wiltshire area and travel to other offices for Meetings and Training). Good basic education, including Maths and English GCSE or equivalent. Experience of proficiently working with Microsoft Office suite including Word and Excel Experience of working with People in the Criminal Justice System and/or disadvantaged people. Knowledge of: local partners/statutory agencies/associated services; An understanding of the importance of risk assessment and management. An understanding of safeguarding adults and children Understanding of emotional well-being support principles Desirable Any qualification relevant to rehabilitation of offenders, for example criminology/ criminal justice/ social care/ mental health/ IAG/ Family Services/ Emotional Wellbeing/ Social Inclusion Additional Information Interview process: Unless otherwise stated, interviews will be arranged as suitable candidates are identified, so early application is strongly advised. Where a deadline is advertised, Catch22 reserves the right to withdraw the post from advertisement without notice. Closing Date: 17:00 on 11th of September 2026. Catch22 reserves the right to withdraw the vacancy at any time, for any reason before the stated closing date. We aim to review applications as quickly as possible. However, due to the volume ofinterest we receive, we may not be able to contact all applicants individually. If you have not heard from us within two weeks of the closing date, please assume that your application has not been successful this time. Shift patterns: Shifts will typically take place between 09:00 and 17:00, however there is a minimum of 1 evening per week required until 19:30. On the day of the late shift you will start later to remain within contractual hours. Benefits 28 days annual leave + bank holidays, rising to 33 days with service. Pension scheme with matching contributions of up to 4% Discounted shopping opportunities Additional Requirements: Successful post-holders will need to have a full UK Driving License and access to a personal vehicle for work purposes. To Apply If you feel you are a suitable candidate and would like to work for Catch22, please do not hesitate to apply.
