item.title: Director, UK People & Culture
item.description: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future. IRC UK IRC UK is part of the IRC global network, which has its global headquarters in New York. Our team in the UK – approximately 220 colleagues – works to raise profile, deliver policy and practice change, and increase funding to help restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Since 2021, IRC UK has also provided integration services directly to refugees across the UK. In Europe, the IRC currently operates in the UK, Germany, Sweden, Belgium, Switzerland, Italy, Greece and Poland. PURPOSE OF THE ROLE The People and Culture (P&C) Director works in a highly matrixed environment with staff from several functions across the global organisation. The postholder manages the HR team in IRC UK and is accountable for effective HR service delivery, HR compliance and continuous improvement within the scope of the People & Culture department, localising the IRC’s global people strategy. This position plays a pivotal role in fostering a positive, inclusive and high-performing workplace culture that aligns with IRC’s values, through exceptional communication skills. The role jointly reports into the UK Executive Director and Regional Director, P&C Europe – with additional reporting accountabilities to the UK Board’s People and Culture Committee. Working within global frameworks set by Global People & Culture, the role localises the implementation of People & Culture priorities and drives UK-specific change initiatives within IRC UK’s culture and regulatory environment. As a member of the UK Senior Management Team (SMT), the role is jointly accountable for the delivery of IRC UK’s Strategic Plan, and has responsibility for the effective delivery of P&C priorities. The Director has a keen focus on building leadership competencies and organisational effectiveness. Success in this role requires the ability to build strong relationships, influence decisions, and navigate multiple stakeholder perspectives to deliver effective people solutions within a matrix environment where accountability is shared. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 1. P&C Leadership (Advisory, Implementation, and Partnering) (25%) As a member of the UK Senior Management Team, assume collective accountability for the effective delivery of IRC UK’s Strategic Plan. Serve as an advisor and thought partner to the Executive Director and fellow SMT members on the UK application of IRC’s Global P&C strategy, and lead on strengthening IRC UK’s kind, inclusive and high-performing organisational culture. Support talent dialogues, performance conversations, and career development planning for IRC UK staff, embedding a culture of continuous learning. Partner with peers on workforce planning — including managing workforce adjustments such as staff reductions or scale-up, and organisational design work — in partnership with senior management, the Regional Director P&C Europe, and Global P&C Partners, ensuring compliance with local and global policy while minimising risk and supporting affected staff. Translate data and metrics into actionable items in line with IRC UK’s strategy. Lead, supervise, and develop the UK P&C team, accountable for team quality and effectiveness and for building a skilled, motivated team ready to advance. 2. Manage HR Service Delivery and Core Operations (~40%) Manage end-to-end HR service delivery across the employee lifecycle; recruitment, onboarding, contracts, payroll coordination, benefits, performance and leave management, offboarding, and HR information systems, maintaining high-quality, context-specific P&C practices aligned with organisational standards. Provide leadership on UK employment law and regulation to the UK HR team, ensuring the HR team supports supervisors of UK staff in the management of their teams in a supportive and compliant way. Provide high quality HR partnership to the Refugee, Asylum and Integration (RAI) UK Director and team to support programme needs and donor requirements. Advise supervisors on appropriate disciplinary actions, coordinating with Global Employee Relations and Legal on complex or escalated disciplinary proceedings, to ensure fairness and compliance with employment law. Responsible for P&C reporting for the UK Board of Trustees and People & Culture Committee, and for the annual production of IRC UK's Gender Pay Gap and Ethnicity Pay Gap reports, in line with IRC's global P&C reporting standards and applicable UK statutory requirements. Support any organisational restructure requirements, including active management of any necessary staff consultation and resulting redundancy processes, by providing expert guidance to management and affected staff throughout the process. Track UK P&C objectives set by Global P&C and contribute HR input - organisational structure, position scoping, staffing analysis - to proposal design and grant review processes. Lead the delivery of regular staff engagement surveys, analysing data and proposing leadership actions in response. 3. Workplace Culture (~15%) Promote employee experience, engagement, and inclusion, and oversee the integration of IRC's Values (the ‘IRC Way’), People Manager Standards, and Employee Success Factors across the employee lifecycle. Implement safeguarding standards set by the global Safeguarding function across hiring and onboarding, and ensure the IRC Way and reporting channels are visible in all IRC UK locations. Serve as a local advocate for Employee Wellbeing, Employee Engagement, and Safeguarding priorities set by global functions, and role model safe, inclusive, and caring leadership standards. Operate and promote collaboration in a highly matrixed environment where several units intersect and work together to reach joint decisions. Accountable for the effective delivery of specific P&C-owned elements of IRC UK's Gender, Equality, Diversity and Inclusion (GEDI) Strategy and Action Plan, as well as assuming joint accountability for the full GEDI Strategy and Action Plan as a key member of IRC UK SMT. 4. Trade Union Relationship (~20%) Working with the UK Executive Director, maintain the relationship with UK Trade Union (Unite) representatives, and negotiate and consult via the quarterly Joint Negotiating Committee (JNC), driving progress on policy and annual salary review negotiations. Develop and manage union engagement and communication plans that support open, honest, and productive dialogue across the office. KEY WORKING RELATIONSHIPS Direct reporting line to UK Executive Director; indirect reporting to Regional Director, P&C Europe UK Board and P&C Committee UK SMT, with particularly close collaboration with Director, Strategy and Delivery, Financial Controller, and RAI UK Director PERSON SPECIFICATION CIPD qualified with significant HR leadership experience across the full P&C spectrum, including complex UK processes such as restructures, TUPE, and employee relations.** Strong interpersonal and analytical skills, with proven ability to operate effectively in a complex, global matrix organisation. Solution-oriented, positive, ‘can do’ attitude. Strong knowledge of UK employment law, with experience of advising and influencing senior leaders.** Experience of working with Trade Unions, including leading on consultations and negotiations.** People management experience.** High level of confidentiality, tact, service orientation, and intercultural communication skills.Ability to manage competing priorities and complex, multi-stakeholder projects independently, with willingness to take on significant responsibility.

item.title: Head of Community Delivery
item.description: Job description We’re looking for an inspiring Head of Community Delivery to join our London-based team. This is a senior leadership role within our Delivery Team, where you’ll play a key part in shaping and delivering AllChild’s place-based programmes, ensuring they create meaningful and lasting impact across your region. Across the UK, millions of children and young people are facing complex social and emotional challenges. AllChild works within local communities and wider support systems to identify and support children and young people most at risk of poor social, emotional and academic outcomes. Through our two-year Impact Programme, we help build a joined-up network of support around each child and family, working in partnership with schools, local services and community organisations. For further information, please view the Job Pack. To apply, please visit our website via the Apply button. Closing date: 25 September 2026. We recognise that candidates may use AI tools to support research and check grammar. However, we ask that all supporting statements and application responses reflect your own thoughts and experiences. Over-reliance on AI may limit our ability to assess your individual skills, critical thinking, and personal approach, which are important parts of our selection process. Posted on: 27 August 2026 Closing date: 25 September 2026 at 23:30 Tags: Training / Learning, Project Management, Compliance / Quality, Delivery, Partnerships, Programme Management, Safeguarding, Students / School, Youth / Children, Governance / Management

item.title: Marketing Officer
item.description: ROLE DESCRIPTION As Marketing Officer, you will report to our External Relations Manager, playing a central role in driving Get Further’s visibility and growth through maintaining our digital platforms and driving campaigns focused on forming and retaining partnerships. You will help Get Further to reach more students by designing and delivering creative multi-channel B2B marketing campaigns that promote our tuition programmes, CPD and curriculum resources to FE colleges, training providers and councils. You will also be responsible for the day-to-day delivery and maintenance of our digital channels, creating compelling written, graphic, photographic and video content, managing our website and email marketing, and using analytics to refine and strengthen performance. Alongside digital delivery, you will contribute to our wider work by creating collateral for and supporting with the delivery of conferences and events, sourcing stories from the students and teachers we support, collaborating with our fundraising and recruitment teams on their campaigns, and supporting our wider team to deliver impactful and brand aligned external communications. Key responsibilities include: Marketing Campaigns & Partnerships Plan and deliver multichannel B2B marketing campaigns that attract new partners and support renewals, using social media (primarily LinkedIn), email marketing, letter campaigns and other channels creatively and strategically. Use audience maps, value propositions and key messaging guides to tailor content to our different audiences (FE colleges, training providers and councils), ensuring alignment with the Get Further brand. Lead the creation of high‑quality marketing collateral (leaflets, banners, videos, case studies, graphics) that strengthens our brand and supports direct sales. Support the planning and delivery of events and campaigns that showcase Get Further’s mission, impact and thought leadership. Use a marketing funnel to track and analyse lead generation and conversion, making data-driven recommendations that allow the marketing and sales teams to improve processes. Coordinate award submissions that raise the organisation’s profile, working with colleagues to compile compelling applications. Digital Content & Platform Management Plan and deliver high‑quality, creative social media content and campaigns that advance our digital strategy and deepen audience engagement. Design engaging graphic and video assets using Canva, Adobe Creative Suite and other tools. Capture high‑quality photo and video content of events and programmes in action. Maintain and update the Get Further website, using WordPress to optimise content, improve user experience and reflect organisational priorities. Support with the creation and publication of blog content, including drafting, editing, proofreading and uploading posts. Track and analyse the performance of digital content and campaigns, using analytics tools to generate insights and recommend data‑driven improvements. Play an active role in shaping our digital content strategy — identifying new opportunities, spotting trends in audience behaviour, and proposing creative approaches to strengthen engagement and reach. Storytelling and impact reporting Support the promotion of Get Further’s impact reports through digital content and event delivery. Work with colleagues to source powerful stories from students and teachers, developing and ensuring all content aligns with our ethical storytelling policy Branding & Team Support Assist colleagues with the design of external documents and assets, ensuring they are user‑friendly, professional and aligned with brand guidelines. Create and maintain written guides, templates, trainings and brand tools that help the team communicate consistently and confidently. Respond to internal requests for branding and communication support. Work with the Fundraising Officer to maintain an organised central library of storytelling assets, including narrative content, photos and videos. Support recruitment campaigns by creating content that showcases the benefits of working at Get Further. Person specification We are seeking a highly-motivated, detail-oriented and creative Marketing Officer who is eager to progress their career in education charity communications. You will be a compelling storyteller who cares deeply about communicating the experiences of the young people and adults we support, and has a strong set of written, video editing and design skills that enable you to tell these stories with clarity and impact. You will be ambitious to take on a leading role in driving our marketing activities, proactively generating and sharing ideas, and bringing a strong set of project management skills that enable you to take ownership on campaigns - from concept, to delivery to evaluation. You will take pride in delivering excellent campaigns and eager to continuously learn and improve. You will have a critical eye for your own work, double and triple checking every aspect to ensure high-quality output, proactively seeking feedback and setting aside time to reflect and evaluate within a busy workload. You will be confident using data to understand performance and analytically minded in using insights to improve both your work and make recommendations for how the wider organisation can improve our strategy and processes. You will be curious to learn about our organisation and audiences, proactively seeking opportunities to learn more about who we are and what we do so that you can communicate about our work to the highest standard and develop a coherent strategic vision for our marketing work. Your strong time management skills will mean that you are comfortable working at pace and have the agility to respond to changing priorities and contexts. For the right candidate, this role offers meaningful opportunities to develop new and existing skills, take on additional responsibilities, and progress internally as you help shape and deliver impactful marketing campaigns that benefit the young people and adults we support. How to apply Your application must include: A CV of no more than 2 sides of A4; and A supporting statement which includes your answers to the following three questions: Why do you want to work for Get Further? (250 words); For the following three areas of the “Role Description” section of the job specification, outline which of your projects/work to date demonstrates that you would be successful in this role: Marketing campaigns & partnerships Digital content & platform management Branding & team support If your application is successful, what two aspects of the role would be the biggest challenge for you, and how would you overcome these challenges? (300 words) Please submit your application via our website by 9am on Thursday 10 September.Incomplete applications will not be processed. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to a first-round interview taking place in the morning on the 15, 16 and 17 of September. Second round interviews will take place week commencing 21 September. This is a UK-based post and applicants must be living in and have the right to work the UK; if applicable please detail your visa status in your covering email. Get Further is an equal opportunities employer and will not discriminate against any candidate on the basis of any characteristic protected by the Equality Act 2010. Please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments to be made throughout the recruitment process. Work Location: Hybrid remote in London

item.title: Shop Manager
item.description: Shop Manager £25,172.40 a year Dartford, DA1 1BZ Would you like to work at the heart of your local community? Are you able to inspire a team of brilliant volunteers? Do you have retail experience and are looking for the next step in your career? If you answered yes to these then we have the perfect opportunity for you. The role Permanent, 35 hours a week. Scope's Dartford shop - 26 High Street, Dartford, DA1 1BZ Please note that successful candidates will be subject to an enhanced DBS check. We welcome all applications by 11:59pm GMT Friday 11 September 2026 As Shop Manager of Scope’s Dartford shop, you’ll have the autonomy to run the shop with creativity and flair. Every day is different. In this role, you’ll lead a team of paid colleagues and volunteers, offering clear guidance, encouragement, and development. Using your experience and management skills, you’ll help grow sales while making sure every customer and donor enjoys a welcoming and inclusive shop experience. In this role you will: • Ensure shop sales performance is maximised, actively seeking ways to improve the shop’s performance on a continuous basis. • Manage all aspects of stock collection and preparation; ensuring that stock processing levels are sufficient to achieve required shop floor density, encouraging stock donations at all times. Also support our online selling with identifying suitable items and listing on online selling platforms • Recruit, manage and develop paid colleagues and volunteers within Scope’s HR and operational policies and procedures and build a strong team • Work collaboratively with the Assistant Shop Manager About you We’re looking for someone who has: • Previous experience as either a Retail Shop Manager, Assistant Manager, or a Supervisor looking to step up, ideally in retail or charity shops. • Commercially aware and able to spot opportunities • Be able to lead and support people • Customer-focused, with a can-do attitude • A team player with strong work ethic • Accurate and detail-oriented • IT literate and numeracy skills We welcome applications from people with lived experience of disability and from all backgrounds. Please include examples in your application that show how your skills, experience, and values match the person specification in the job description. We also ask you to share how you support Scope’s values and contribute to our goal of creating a fair and equal future for disabled people. Working in Our Shops Our shops are the face of our retail brand, run by dedicated, creative, and passionate teams. We focus on sustainable fashion, engage with local communities, and lead volunteers to deliver a great experience for colleagues and customers. Funds raised support Scope’s mission of achieving equality for disabled people and their families. Shop Hours Scope shops are open every day. Some weekend and Bank Holiday cover is needed. Full-time: 35 hours per week, five days out of seven Part-time: Weekly hours on a seven-day rota Additional information In line with UK legislation, we are only able to accept applications from individuals aged 18 or over. This is because the role may involve working alone in the shop without other staff present. You must be eligible to work in the UK to apply for this vacancy. Scope is not able to offer visa sponsorship. Anonymised applications We use an anonymised application process to support our commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion. All applicants must submit an anonymised CV and complete a short online application form. Our values Pioneering, Courageous, Connected, Open, Fair. We trust each other and give colleagues freedom to be creative, push boundaries, and change minds. Our promise to disabled people We are proud to be a charity that stands for disability equality. We welcome applications from disabled people and anyone with an impairment, condition, or access need. We want our team to reflect the communities we serve. As a Disability Confident Leader, we promise to offer an interview to all disabled applicants who meet the essential requirements for the job. To do this, tick the box in your application to say you are applying under the Offer an Interview Scheme (this used to be called the Guaranteed Interview Scheme). If you need any changes or support during the recruitment process, please email us via our website. You can also find more details about asking for adjustments at interview on our website. Important to know You must meet all the essential requirements listed in the job description. If lots of people apply, we may need to limit interviews to a fair number of disabled applicants who best meet the criteria. Equality, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) EDI is a priority at Scope. We welcome applications from people of colour and other underrepresented communities. We aim to create a culture where everyone feels they belong, treating all with dignity and respect. As a disability equality charity, accessibility and inclusion come first. We listen, learn and continuously improve. You can find out more about our approach to Equality, Diversity and Inclusion on the Scope website. item.title: Oxford & Thames Valley Peer Support Lead
item.description: Are you passionate about reducing health inequalities and supporting some of the most marginalised people in our communities? We are recruiting for a compassionate, organised, and proactive Peer Support Lead to support our hepatitis C peer project in the Oxford & Thames Valley area. Peers use their lived experience to raise awareness of hepatitis C, reduce stigma, and help people access testing and treatment. Working alongside healthcare professionals, drug and alcohol services, homelessness services, and community organisations, you will recruit, train and support volunteer peers to deliver hepatitis C awareness raising, practical and emotional support. This is a varied and rewarding community-based position involving travel across the Oxford and Thames Valley region. About you We are looking for someone who can build trust and engage people with complex needs in a respectful, non-judgemental way. You’ll be a good communicator, confident working with partner services and supporting volunteers, with good organisational skills and an understanding of confidentiality, professional boundaries and managing risk. We welcome applications from people with either lived experience or professional experience relevant to the role. This may include hepatitis C, drug or alcohol use, homelessness, the criminal justice system, or supporting people facing similar challenges. Why join us? The Hepatitis C Trust is a national, patient-led charity committed to eliminating hepatitis C and improving access to harm reduction services across the UK. We are proud to be a Living Wage Employer and are committed to equality, diversity and inclusion. How to apply The closing date for applications is midnight, Sunday 27th September 2026 .

item.title: Data Curator
item.description: Within commutable distance of Beckenham, Birmingham, Blackburn, Doncaster, Redcar, Bristol or Bradford 12-month fixed term contract At the National Institute of Teaching (NIoT), we believe teaching is a fundamental societal good, a privilege and a responsibility. We are on a mission to improve the quality of teacher and leader development at a system level, using evidence, research and partnership to help shape a stronger education system for the future. This is an exciting opportunity to join an organisation with a clear and ambitious mission. Our work brings together high-quality programme delivery, rigorous research and deep sector knowledge to generate and apply insights that can improve teaching and learning across the country. The data we collect through our programmes and partnerships is central to that mission: it helps us understand what works, strengthen professional development, and ensure evidence informs practice, policy and public debate. About the role As Data Curator, you will play a key role in making sure our data can be used safely, effectively and insightfully to support research and generate impact. You will work across teams to understand how data is generated, how it is currently used, and how systems, processes and tools can be strengthened so that our data is reliable, accessible and fit for research purposes. You will work closely with colleagues behind the NIoT’s Teacher Education Dataset (TED), helping to maintain and enhance curated datasets and explore how new sources of data can strengthen our understanding of teacher and leader development. You will also collaborate with researchers and practitioners working through the NIoT’s Professional Development Laboratory, our test-and-learn centre focused on identifying and sharing effective approaches to professional development. This role would suit someone who enjoys working at the intersection of data, research and education, and who is motivated by the opportunity to contribute to work that has real sector-wide significance. This role is fixed term due to funding, and it is too early to comment on the possibility of a permanent position. This is a hybrid role, with the requirement for in person working for a minimum of once a fortnight, occasionally this will be more due to business need. The role includes participation in our annual all-staff away day (including an overnight stay) and occasional national travel. We think a wide range of different work and educational experiences could support you to be successful in this role. We encourage applications from all backgrounds, communities and industries, and are committed to employing a team that has diverse skills, experiences and abilities. Essential Criteria : Commitment to the NIoT’s mission and to improving outcomes through rigorous evidence, strong partnerships and thoughtful external engagement. Experience working with data in an education context, such as school, MAT, university, or teacher education settings. Experience applying data quality concepts — completeness, consistency, accuracy – in professional and/or research contexts. Experience of applying data governance principles in school and/or research settings. Experience interrogating and working with structured datasets, with or without technical coding skills. Familiarity with the use of qualitative and quantitative data for research purposes, as well as key issues in data interpretation such as biases and comparability. Ability to learn and adapt quickly and take initiative in the face of new challenges. Strong communication skills with the ability to communicate clearly about data to expert and non-expert audiences, adhering to high professional standards. Strong ability to work both collaboratively and independently. Motivated to work at the interface of academic and professional priorities and working cultures, with a diverse team and multiple external stakeholders. Desirable Criteria : Degree level education, or equivalent experience. Experience working as a teacher or in another professional role in schools, such as data manager. Familiarity with school data systems (MIS systems like Bromcom, SIMS, Arbor) Strong documentation skills such as writing data dictionaries, process documentation, and data flow mapping Understanding of data linking concepts and the challenges involved Knowledge of GDPR and data sharing in an education context Experience with tools like Excel, SQL, R, Python or GitHub at a basic level Degree in a relevant field such as data science, information management, education, social science, or a related discipline Evidence of continuing professional development in data management (e.g. CDMP, or relevant training) Key Benefits: Highly competitive pay and pay progression opportunities Flexible start and end working times Flexible working opportunities, including hybrid working At least 27 days’ holiday a year (plus 8 bank holidays) rising to 33 days after five years’ service Entry to the Local Government Pension Scheme A stimulating, supportive and rewarding working environment with a dedicated team of likeminded professionals Excellent opportunities to develop your skills and experience and to progress your career For more information and to apply, please visit our vacancies page. Closing date: 4.00pm on 18 September 2026. Interview date: w/c 28 September 2026. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if we receive a high volume of applications. Candidates must already have the right to work in the UK, as we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role. This post requires a satisfactory enhanced disclosure from the Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) with a Children’s Barred List Check and Occupational Health Check is required as a condition of employment .
item.dc:creator: National Institute of Teaching

item.title: Digital Innovation and Development Manager
item.description: Are you excited by the potential of digital technology and data to make a real difference in people's lives? Community Action Redbridge is looking for a creative, forward-thinking Digital Innovation and Development Manager to lead the next stage of our digital journey and help shape how technology supports communities across one of London's most diverse boroughs. Redbridge is home to vibrant communities and a dynamic voluntary, community and social enterprise (VCSE) sector. We want to harness the power of digital technology and data to strengthen communities, support local VCSE organisations and help create a fairer Redbridge. Working across the organisation, you'll lead the implementation of our ambitious Digital Innovation and Development Strategy. You'll help create more consistent and effective systems that reduce duplication, improve collaboration and enable our team to focus on what matters most: supporting our communities and member organisations. You'll champion a data-driven culture, helping us turn information into insight, better understand our impact, and make informed decisions that respond to emerging needs. You'll play a key role in building digital confidence across the organisation, empowering staff to embrace new technologies, develop their skills and use digital tools effectively in their everyday work. Beyond Community Action Redbridge, you'll work directly with local charities and community groups to strengthen their digital capacity, improve access to data and insight, and foster stronger connections across Redbridge's VCSE sector. If you're excited by the power of digital technology to connect people, improve services and create lasting social impact, we'd love to hear from you. About Community Action Redbridge Community Action Redbridge is a local infrastructure organisation dedicated to building a fairer Redbridge where everyone and every community has an equal opportunity to thrive. Our work supports the development of strong and resilient communities where people lead happy, healthy, and fulfilling lives. At the heart of our work is a commitment to social justice and to tackling the root causes of inequality. We’re passionate about shifting power, amplifying community voices and working collaboratively to create social change. We do this by: What it’s like to work at Community Action Redbridge We’re committed to creating a truly inclusive workplace culture that embraces and celebrates difference. Building a team that reflects the diversity of our communities and brings together a range of experiences, backgrounds and perspectives is essential to the work we do. We want Community Action Redbridge to be a safe space for everyone to bring their whole selves to work, where all our employees have the opportunity to thrive and feel recognised and valued for the work they do. We offer some great benefits including 28 days’ annual leave (including the festive closure period) plus public holidays, a free and confidential employee helpline, face-to-face and telephone counselling, and a travel loan and cycle to work scheme. How to apply Please submit your CV and a covering letter answering the following 4 questions (no more than 500 words each): Describe a digital transformation, systems improvement or innovation project that you have led. What was the challenge, what approach did you take, and what impact did it have on the organisation, team or service users? Why do you want to join Community Action Redbridge, and how do your values, skills and experience equip you to help us use digital technology to strengthen communities and create positive social change? Please apply directly through the CharityJob website by midnight on Monday 28th September 2026. First-stage interviews will take place online on Tuesday 6th October 2026. Candidates successfully shortlisted from the first stage will be invited to attend a second-stage interview in person, which is expected to take place on Tuesday 13th October 2026. If you would like an informal conversation about the role before applying, please email us directly to arrange a suitable time.

As our second-in-command, you’ll work closely with our Chief Officer, trustees and leadership team. item.title: Side-by-Side Community Engagement Worker
item.description: About the role The Side-by-Side project supports children in care and care leavers to have the same opportunities as those who have not experienced care. For many young people, navigating the care system and especially the transition to leaving care can be complex, isolating, and overwhelming. Too often, care-experienced young people are expected to face adulthood before they are ready, without the safety nets of family, friends, and community networks that many of us take for granted. The project provides a mentoring and befriending service, offering consistent, trusted relationships that help young people feel less alone, build confidence and life skills, and navigate key life changes as they move towards independence. Side-by-Side supports young people with a range of needs, including those who may be at risk of exploitation, unaccompanied asylum-seeking children, and young people living with identified mental health challenges. The project is guided by strong safeguarding practice, built on trust, and delivered through trauma-informed, person-centred approaches. Working 18 hours per week, you will work directly with young people through engagement sessions, group activities and co-designed initiatives. You will also work alongside volunteers, supporting them to safely and effectively engage with young people. This role does not involve acting as a young person’s key worker or holding a caseload. Instead your focus is on enabling connections, strengthening community networks and creating opportunities for young people to thrive across Solihull. Please note this is a fixed term contract position for 12 months. About you We are looking for a compassionate and motivated individual with strong local knowledge and a commitment to community-based support. You will be confident working directly with care-experienced young people, including those who may be at risk of exploitation, unaccompanied asylum-seeking children, and young people living with identified mental health challenges. Your key responsibilities will include: Build community links: develop relationships with local venues, services, and partners to support young people and Side-by-Side activities. Support volunteers: recruit, train, and guide volunteers, helping them signpost young people to relevant services. Engage young people: deliver activities, gather feedback, and support co-designed initiatives to ensure young people shape the services they receive. Live our values: all work is guided by trust, reducing loneliness, providing practical and emotional support, and delivering person-centred approaches. Employee benefits We offer the following employee benefits: 26 days, increasing to 30 days annual leave plus bank holidays (pro rata for part time) Occupational sick pay (subject to completion of qualifying period) Enhanced pay for family friendly leave Free parking at some of our offices Employee assistance programme Group stakeholder pension scheme Access to BHSF health cash plan Cycle to work scheme Support and supervision from your line manager Learning and Development opportunities How to apply Please visit our website for the job description and to apply. In your application, you will need to evidence, using specific examples, how your skills and experience meet the criteria laid out in the person specification, within the job description attached. The interview date will be confirmed and are expected to take place in person in Solihull Safeguarding and Compliance NYAS operates robust safe procedures to ensure the protection of the children, young people and adults at risk we work with. To comply with NYAS’s Safeguarding and Child Protection Policy, candidates will be subject to an enhanced DBS check, references and a Digital Risk Assessment. In accordance with UK immigration law, NYAS is required to ensure that all prospective candidates have the legal right to work in the United Kingdom. Therefore, proof of eligibility to work in the UK will be required as part of the recruitment process. We reserve the right to close the advert early should the right candidate be found before the closing date. About NYAS As an established leading rights-based charity, NYAS (National Youth Advocacy Service) is well positioned to ensure that children, young people, and adults across England and Wales are fully respected, represented, and supported in expressing their views and having their rights upheld. We work with care-experienced children, young people, and adults who are often reliant on statutory services suffering the negative impact of the cuts in public expenditure. Our combination of social care and legal services places us in a unique position to ensure that they receive the services they need and that their voices are heard. We are an equal opportunities employer and we are committed to creating an inclusive environment which means NYAS welcomes applications from all individuals regardless of age, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, ethnic origin, nationality, religion or belief, or any other protected characteristic. NYAS is proud to share that we are a Disability Confident Employer and we guarantee to interview all disabled applicants who meet the minimum criteria for our vacancies. Work with us to help change young lives.

item.description: Job Title: Interim Research and Policy Lead Contract: Temporary contract - Maternity cover (13 months) Hours: 21 hours per week Salary: £21,600 per annum (£36,000 FTE) Location: Hybrid (Home Based/London) About Coram Coram is committed to improving the lives of the UK’s most vulnerable children and young people. We support children and young people from birth to independence, creating a change that lasts a lifetime. Coram is the UK’s oldest children’s charity founded by Thomas Coram in London helping vulnerable children and young people since 1739. Today, the Coram group helps more than one million children, young people, families and professionals every year by providing access to the skills and opportunities they need to thrive. About Coram PACEY Coram PACEY (previously the Professional Association for Childcare and Early Years) was formed in 1977, we are a professional association dedicated to supporting home-based childcare professionals including childminders and nannies to provide high quality services, information and advice to children, their families and carers. We want all children to experience high quality childcare and early education, helping them to have a bright future. About the role The purpose of this role is to lead Coram PACEY’s programme of policy and campaigning activity planned during an important year for Coram PACEY as we celebrate our 50th anniversary. This will include a landmark piece of research into the future of childminding, this is an exciting time to join the organisation. As Maternity Cover Policy and Research Lead, this role will be key in developing and delivering Coram PACEY’s policy priorities and campaigns providing expertise across key policy areas, support the Head of Coram PACEY to represent members’ concerns, and work with decision-makers, campaigners and partners to influence meaningful change for childminders, home-based childcare professionals and the wider early years sector. To apply for this role, please click on the 'apply now' button below to complete the application. Closing Date: 13th September 2026 Interview Date: 21st September 2026 Coram is an equal opportunities employer and we believe a diverse workforce enables us to improve the services to the children and families we help. We are genuinely committed to encouraging candidates from all sections of the community we seek to support. This includes those from global majority ethnic backgrounds, those that identify as LGBQT+, those with disabilities, those with lived experience of care, those with neuro-diversity, and those from other groups who are underrepresented at Coram. If applicants feel comfortable, we would encourage them to draw on lived experience as well as professional experience in their personal statement as part of their application. We are committed to the safeguarding of children and where appropriate will require the successful applicant to undertake a check from the Disclosure and Barring Service. item.title: Executive Director
item.description: Help lead the next chapter of an award-winning, volunteer-powered environmental charity As we celebrate our 10-year anniversary, Shrewsbury Food Hub is looking for an inclusive, practical and strategically minded Executive Director to lead us through the next phase of our development. We have a simple vision: a community where food is valued and not wasted. Founded in 2016, we rescue surplus food seven days a week from local suppliers and redistribute it through charities, community groups, schools and Foodshares. In the year to March 2026 alone, we rescued more than 270 tonnes of food, with our work reaching an estimated 4,000 people every week across Shrewsbury and the surrounding area. We have also developed a growing programme of community cooking, bringing people together to build skills and confidence, share food and strengthen community – while ensuring that good food does not go to waste. The opportunity Shrewsbury Food Hub has grown significantly over the past decade. Our next Executive Director will help us build on that success while strengthening the foundations beneath it. This is an exciting opportunity to lead an established and much-loved local charity through a period of organisational development: bringing greater clarity, focus, structure and resilience while protecting the energy, relationships and community spirit that make the Hub special. The Board is committed to focusing increasingly on governance and delegating day-to-day leadership and management to the Executive Director. You will have the authority and responsibility to lead the organisation, work closely with our Senior Leadership Team and create the conditions in which staff and volunteers can perform at their best. This is not a figurehead role. We need an Executive Director who can see the bigger picture, make difficult choices and turn strategy into practical action – someone equally comfortable around the Board table and spending time with the staff, volunteers and partners who make our work possible. This role is largely based in Shrewsbury, with some home working possible. This is a strongly place-based role requiring a regular and visible on-site presence. What you will lead Working with the Board, staff, volunteers and partners, you will: Lead the development and delivery of a clear, focused and financially sustainable strategy. Strengthen our structures, systems, processes and ways of working, leading organisational change with clarity and sensitivity. Provide overall leadership for safe, reliable and effective operations and organisational risk. Build an inclusive, enabling and accountable culture, supporting and developing our Senior Leadership Team and wider community of staff and volunteers. Oversee financial sustainability and the development of a strong, balanced income base. Build trusted relationships with funders, suppliers, businesses, local authorities and community partners, acting as a visible and credible ambassador for the Hub. Please see the full Job Description and Person Specification for further details. Who are we looking for? You will bring successful senior leadership experience from a charity, social enterprise, public service or other purpose-led organisation, together with experience of shaping strategy, leading change and turning plans into results. You will be financially astute, pragmatic and comfortable creating clarity in a busy organisation. Above all, you will be a genuine people leader : emotionally intelligent, approachable and able to build trust across a diverse community of staff, volunteers, trustees, founders and partners. We don't expect our new Executive Director to be a specialist in everything. You may bring particular depth in operational and organisational leadership or in income generation, fundraising and external development . What matters is that you have credible experience of the other and the leadership ability to bring different expertise together. Previous Executive Director experience is welcome, but is not essential. Our values We want our new Executive Director to share our commitment to reducing food waste and strengthening our community, and to lead in a way that reflects our values: Passion – Accountability – Inclusiveness – Integrity – Caring – Resilience These values shape not only what we do, but how we work together. We are looking for a leader who enables others to succeed, listens to different perspectives, acts with integrity and empathy, and remains purposeful and constructive through change. Our ambitions remain firmly rooted in place. We believe there is significant potential to deepen our environmental and social impact across Shrewsbury and Shropshire , rather than becoming a national organisation. How to apply: Please submit your CV and a covering letter of no more than three pages , outlining your suitability for the role, by 5pm on Friday 25 September 2026 . Shortlisted candidates will be invited to visit Shrewsbury Food Hub on Monday 5 October 2026 , providing an opportunity to meet the team, see the Hub in action and gain a deeper understanding of the organisation ahead of formal interviews. Shrewsbury Food Hub values the strength that comes from different experiences and perspectives. item.title: Interim Director of Finance and Operations
item.description: Interim Director of Finance & Operations - 6 months contract September 2026 Start | 4 Days per Week | £75,000-£80,000 FTE (£60,000-£64,000 Pro Rata) | High Wycombe & Hybrid Working Charity People are delighted to be partnering with a respected and impactful charity with an annual income of approximately £4.5 million to recruit an Interim Director of Finance & Operations. This is a pivotal senior leadership opportunity for an experienced finance and operations professional who is passionate about supporting organisational effectiveness and enabling impactful charitable work. Reporting directly to the Interim CEO and working closely with Trustees and senior colleagues, you will provide strategic leadership across Finance, HR, IT, Facilities, Data & Insights, Compliance and Programme Support. As a key member of the Senior Leadership Team, you will be responsible for ensuring the organisation operates with strong financial stewardship, effective governance, robust risk management and high-quality operational support. You will play a vital role in shaping organisational priorities, supporting informed decision-making and creating the conditions that enable colleagues and services to thrive. This is an excellent opportunity to join a values-driven organisation where you can make a significant contribution while leading a broad and varied portfolio of central services. Key Responsibilities Provide strategic leadership for financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting and financial management across the organisation. Deliver insightful financial and operational reporting to the CEO, Senior Leadership Team and Board, supporting effective decision-making and organisational performance. Lead and develop the Finance, HR, IT, Facilities, Data & Insights, Compliance and Programme Support functions, ensuring effective delivery against organisational priorities. Oversee annual business planning, performance monitoring and resource planning processes, ensuring organisational objectives are effectively translated into operational delivery. Support budget holders to strengthen financial understanding, accountability and ownership across the organisation. Lead organisational risk management, maintaining effective controls and ensuring appropriate mitigation strategies are in place. Ensure compliance with Charity Commission requirements, SORP, data protection legislation and other relevant regulatory frameworks Lead the organisation's internal audit approach and oversee external audit and statutory reporting processes. Provide strategic oversight of HR, workforce planning, people development and organisational culture, helping to create an inclusive and high-performing working environment. Oversee IT, systems, data and supplier relationships, ensuring the organisation has the infrastructure and support required to operate effectively and efficiently. Drive continuous improvement across systems, policies and operational processes, ensuring services remain effective, efficient and aligned to organisational needs. Lead procurement and contract management activities, ensuring value for money and strong commercial oversight. About You We are seeking a collaborative and commercially minded leader (with strong charity / NFP experience) who combines strategic thinking with strong operational delivery. You will bring: A recognised CCAB qualification (ACA, ACCA, CIMA or CIPFA). Significant senior-level finance leadership experience within the charity or not-for-profit sector. Strong understanding of charity finance, governance, Charity Commission requirements and the Charities SORP framework. Experience leading finance alongside broader central services functions, including HR, IT, Facilities, Compliance and Operations. Experience working closely with Boards, Trustees and senior leadership teams. Strong financial planning, reporting and analytical capability. The ability to balance strategic oversight with a practical, hands-on approach. Excellent communication, influencing and stakeholder management skills. A supportive leadership style with a track record of developing teams and building organisational capability. What's on Offer? A highly influential Senior Leadership Team role within a respected and purpose-driven organisation. The opportunity to work closely with the CEO, Board and senior colleagues. A broad and rewarding portfolio spanning finance, operations, governance and corporate services. A flexible 4-day working week. Hybrid working, with 1-2 days per week in the High Wycombe office. The opportunity to make an immediate and meaningful impact from September 2026. Contract Details Salary: £75,000-£80,000 FTE (£60,000-£64,000 pro rata) Contract: 6-month fixed-term contract, 28 hours per week across 4 days Start Date: ASAP (September 2026) Location: High Wycombe, Buckinghamshire. Office attendance required 1-2 days per week. How to Apply Due to the immediate nature of this appointment, applications will close on 1 September 2026, with interviews taking place shortly thereafter. Candidates who are available at short notice and able to commence the assignment in September 2026 are particularly encouraged to apply. Charity People is a forward‑thinking, inclusive organisation that deliberately champions equity, diversity and inclusion. We know charities thrive when inclusion is at the centre of decision‑making. We proudly match organisations with talent based on skills and values, not background - because diverse teams deliver stronger results.

item.title: Digital Analyst
item.description: Digital Analyst Are you a digital analyst who enjoys getting into the data, understanding what people do online and turning that insight into action? Great Ormond Street Hospital Charity is looking for a Digital Analyst to help us better understand our supporters and improve the performance of our digital campaigns and experiences. Working across Fundraising and closely with colleagues in Marketing and Technology, you'll bring together data from across our digital channels to understand what's working, what's not and where we can make things better. From campaign performance and supporter journeys your insight will help teams make confident, evidence-led decisions. This is a hands-on role for someone who is technically curious but also enjoys working with people. This is the ideal role for someone who can dig into GA4, GTM and data one moment and translate what they've found into a clear recommendations. Salary The salary for this role is £42,770 per annum and we operate a hybrid working policy of a minimum of 2 days per week in the office. In line with our EDI strategy and Total Reward policy, we calculate our salaries based on benchmarking data across the charity sector. To ensure fairness for existing staff and new joiners, we do not offer salaries above the advertised rate. Key Responsibilities Analyse performance across digital campaigns, websites and supporter journeys, turning data into clear insights and recommendations. Work closely with Marketing and Fundraising teams throughout the campaign lifecycle, helping teams understand performance and identify opportunities to optimise activity. Maintain and improve our GA4 and Google Tag Manager implementation, ensuring tracking and measurement are accurate and useful. Build dashboards and reporting that make digital performance easy for colleagues to understand and use. Analyse supporter behaviour to identify opportunities to improve conversion, engagement, retention and the overall digital experience. Plan and evaluate A/B and multivariate tests, helping us develop a curious, evidence-led approach to improving digital performance. Work with developers, agencies and Technology colleagues to implement and maintain digital tracking across our digital estate. Collaborate with other analysts to connect digital insight with our wider understanding of fundraising and supporter behaviour. Help ensure digital data is collected responsibly and transparently, including supporting GDPR and cookie consent requirements. Keep curious about developments in digital analytics, measurement and technology, bringing useful ideas and improvements back into the organisation. Skills, Knowledge and Expertise Strong hands-on experience with Google Analytics 4 and Google Tag Manager, including implementing and maintaining digital measurement and tracking. Experience using SQL to interrogate and analyse data. Experience working with JavaScript and HTML within Google Tag Manager to implement tracking solutions. Strong digital analytics skills, with experience analysing website, campaign or customer/supporter behaviour and translating findings into actionable recommendations. Understanding of digital marketing channels such as paid media, email, social and organic search, and how analytics can help improve their performance. Experience creating dashboards, visualisations and performance reporting that help others make decisions. Experience supporting experimentation and optimisation through A/B testing or other testing approaches. Strong communication and stakeholder skills, with the ability to make complex data understandable and relevant to different audiences. A collaborative approach and confidence working across multidisciplinary teams including Marketing, Digital, Fundraising and Technology. Strong attention to detail and a curious, analytical mindset—you enjoy asking why something happened, not just reporting that it did. This is an opportunity to use your technical expertise to make data genuinely useful—helping teams understand our supporters, test new ideas and create better digital experiences that inspire people to engage with and support our work. DBS - note a Basic DBS check is required for this role.
item.dc:creator: Great Ormond Street Hospital Children's Charity

item.title: Reporting Analyst
item.description: Are you a Reporting Analyst who enjoys turning complex data into clear, useful information that helps people make better decisions? Great Ormond Street Hospital Charity is looking for a Reporting Analyst to develop the dashboards, reporting and performance information used by teams across Fundraising, Marketing and the wider organisation. This is a hands-on role where you'll combine Power BI, SQL and analytical thinking with lots of stakeholder interaction. You'll build and improve reporting, understand what colleagues really need from their data and find smarter ways to make trusted information easier to access and use. Salary The salary for this role is £42,770 per annum and we operate a hybrid working policy of a minimum of 2 days per week in the office. In line with our EDI strategy and Total Reward policy, we calculate our salaries based on benchmarking data across the charity sector. To ensure fairness for existing staff and new joiners, we do not offer salaries above the advertised rate. Key Responsibilities Build, maintain and improve Power BI dashboards and reporting that help teams understand performance and make informed decisions. Use SQL and multiple data sources to interrogate, validate and prepare data for reporting and analysis. Work with colleagues across the charity to understand their questions and translate them into useful reporting and business intelligence solutions. Develop clear KPIs and performance measures that give teams a consistent view of what is happening and where attention is needed. Turn data into clear, engaging reporting that makes complex information easier for different audiences to understand. Work alongside our Data Engineering and Analysis teams to develop the datasets and reporting capabilities colleagues need. Identify opportunities to automate and simplify reporting, reducing manual processes and making information easier to access. Support colleagues to confidently use dashboards and self-service reporting, helping make data part of everyday decision-making. Help maintain high standards of data quality, accuracy and governance across our reporting. Skills, Knowledge and Expertise Strong hands-on experience developing dashboards and reporting using Power BI. Strong SQL skills, with experience interrogating, analysing and validating large datasets. Experience working with multiple data sources to produce accurate and meaningful business intelligence. Strong analytical and numerical skills, with the ability to spot trends and understand what the data is telling you. Experience developing KPIs, performance measures or reporting frameworks. Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to understand what colleagues need and translate this into practical reporting solutions. Good communication skills, including the ability to present data and explain findings clearly to non-technical audiences. A proactive approach to improving and automating reporting processes. Experience of fundraising, supporter or charity data would be useful, but isn't essential. This is an opportunity to help make data easier to understand, easier to access and more useful. You’ll enable colleagues to have the confidence to turn information into action. DBS - note a Basic DBS check is required for this role.

item.title: Welfare Benefits Caseworker
item.description: “Providing free, independent, confidential and impartial advice” Citizens Advice Southwark has a track record of delivering high-quality services from its offices in Peckham and Walworth and outreach locations across Southwark and South East London. We sort out problems together, for good, by providing free, independent, confidential and impartial advice across all areas of social welfare law, and through using the experience of our clients to bring about positive change through research and campaigns. Citizens Advice Southwark provides outreach advice service in hospitals across South East London as well as from our main offices in Peckham and Walworth. We are seeking to recruit a welfare benefits caseworker to undertake casework assisting clients to access their entitlements to welfare benefits and other sources of financial help. To be successful you will need: At least one year’s full time (or part time equivalent) paid or unpaid recent experience of advice work. This should include advising and undertaking casework on complex cases in social welfare law. Demonstrable in-depth knowledge of welfare benefits including those related to disability and sickness. An understanding of and commitment to the Aims and Principles of the Citizens Advice service including Equal Opportunities policies. Closing date: 9.00am Monday 14 September 2026 Interviews: Friday 18 September 2026 We offer a range of employee benefits, including generous annual leave, an employer matched pension contribution up to 10% salary, and training and development opportunities to continue your professional development. Citizens Advice Southwark is an equal opportunities employer and encourages applications from all applicants who meet the person specification irrespective of sex, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership status, pregnancy and maternity, sexual orientation, race, religion or belief, age, or disability.

item.title: Bid Writer
item.description: Job description The postholder will be responsible for identifying, writing, and submitting compelling, well-researched and tailored funding applications to relevant grant-giving bodies. The post holder will work closely with the LDHAS management team to gather information, write bids, and track progress of submissions, ensuring LDHAS meets income targets as agreed by the Trustees. The postholder will: Proactively research, navigate the system and identify suitable grant and funding opportunities from charitable trusts, foundations, and statutory bodies. Write and submit high-quality funding applications and proposals in line with LDHAS's strategic priorities working closely with the Manager and in their collaboration with key partners. Work collaboratively with the LDHAS Manager and colleagues to gather accurate, up-to-date data and service information for applications. Tailor applications to funder requirements and priorities, ensuring persuasive storytelling and alignment with LDHAS 's mission. Research and identify opportunities to raise money via businesses including payroll giving and sponsoring fundraising events. Research and identify opportunities to encourage supporters to consider leaving a gift to LDHAS in their wills. Manage a pipeline of applications and submissions, ensuring deadlines are met and income targets are tracked. Communication and Relationships Have communication skills and a communication style which ensures that written bids are compelling, clear, and rooted in evidence. Ability to turn service data and case studies into powerful narratives that align with funder priorities. Act as an ambassador for vulnerable people. Maintain effective communication with the Board Analytical and judgement skills Research and identify suitable grant and funding opportunities from charitable trusts, foundations, and statutory bodies. Work collaboratively with LDHAS Manager and colleagues to gather accurate, up-to-date data and service information for applications. Planning and organisation skills Contributes to LDHAS's long-term income generation plans. Manage a pipeline of applications and submissions, ensuring deadlines are met and income targets are tracked. Manage LDHAS’s bid writing schedule ensuring effective systems and accountability. Support development of strong internal bid and grant management systems, including templates, case studies, and project reporting tools. Monitor success rates and provide monthly performance reporting. Client care Assist clients during incidental contacts. Provide general, non-clinical advice to clients. Provide general advice tomembers of public contacting LDHAS. Responsibilities for policy and service development Lead on Bid writing policy and procedure development. Proposes changes to improve LDHAS practice, policies and action plans. Responsibilities for Finance / physical resources Ensure equipment required for the role is appropriate and used safely. Manage finances associated with the role. Responsibility for human resources Demonstrate own duties to other staff Promote a positive and supportive culture. Responsibility for information resources Production of monthly and quarterly management reports to senior management. Preparation of year-end status report. Research and development Assist with audits as required and ensure regulatory compliance Personal development To actively participate in continued professional development to develop new skills, maintain and update existing skills and embrace the concept of Lifelong Learning. To identify appropriate training opportunities in line with identified needs. To be responsible for own continuing professional development and maintaining own professional registration maintaining a professional portfolio and demonstrating evidence of reflective practice. To undertake mandatory training and attend updates and study days as appropriate to the post. Freedom to act The post holder will have the freedom to take action based on own interpretation of broad professional policies, new developments, emerging evidence. The postholder will advise the Board seeking advice as necessary. Other: Promote the work of LDHAS where appropriate Carry out any other work or duties that are reasonably requested Posted on: 27 August 2026 Closing date: 25 September 2026 at 14:00 Tags: Fundraising, Content Writing / Copywriting, Data Analysis, Homelessness, Social Media, Community Fundraising, Corporate Fundraising, Individual Giving, Digital Fundraising, Grants The client requests no contact from agencies or media sales.

item.title: Individual Giving and Legacy Lead
item.description: Job description The Seafarers’ Charity is the leader in maritime welfare grant-making. For over 100 years we have led the way in supporting those who work at sea. We are looking for an Individual Giving and Legacy Lead who will play a key role in building meaningful, long-term relationships with supporters, helping them feel connected to The Seafarers' Charity's mission and the difference their generosity makes to seafarers and their families. Through thoughtful engagement, excellent stewardship and a deep understanding of supporter motivations, the role will develop meaningful supporter journeys across individual giving, legacy giving, in-memory giving and other supporter-led income streams. By creating positive experiences that foster trust, loyalty and advocacy, the postholder will strengthen long-term support for the charity and contribute to sustainable income growth. item.title: Senior Data Insight Analyst
item.description: About the role We’re looking for a Senior Data Insight Analyst to be the lead analyst and data product owner dedicated to our Support and Influencing directorate. You’ll develop high-quality reporting, analysis and data products that help colleagues understand service performance, improve access and equity, and demonstrate the impact of our services, policy and influencing work. Working across the Data team and closely with Support and Influencing colleagues, you’ll lead the development of consistent data collection processes, KPI definitions and analytical frameworks. You’ll turn complex data into clear, actionable insight that supports service design, strategic planning, evaluation, partnerships and decision-making across the charity. About you You’ll bring extensive experience in data analysis and BI development, with a strong track record of leading end-to-end reporting and analysis in complex organisations. You’ll be confident working with multiple datasets and data sources, developing reporting and analytics roadmaps with stakeholders, and presenting findings clearly to non-technical audiences. You’ll have strong skills in SQL and Excel, alongside experience using BI and data visualisation tools such as Power BI, Tableau or similar. You’ll be a collaborative problem-solver who can navigate ambiguity, build trusted relationships, champion data quality and help others feel confident using data and insight to improve services and outcomes. Job description and benefits The job description and our attractive benefits are available for you to download. Primary location of role and hybrid working This role is primarily based in our London or Sheffield office. Our hybrid working model allows you to work up to 3 days per week at home. Some occasional travel between offices may be required. The salary range is: £42,000 to £46,000 per annum if London-based £38,000 to £42,000 per annum if Sheffield based When applying We hope you choose to apply for this role. To support your application, you’ll be asked to submit your anonymised CV and a supporting statement. Please refer to the essential criteria on the person specification and clearly provide as much information as you can with examples, to demonstrate how and where you meet the criteria. If you’ve any immediate questions please contact the Breast Cancer Now recruitment team Our commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion We’re committed to promoting equity, valuing diversity and creating an inclusive environment – for everyone who works for us, works with us, supports us and who we support. We reserve the right to close this advert early. Therefore, to avoid disappointment please submit your application as soon as possible, if you’re interested in this opportunity. item.title: Benefits Advice Officer - No Experience Required
item.description: Join Our Team and Help Transform Lives! We are looking for a compassionate and motivated Benefits Adviser to join our Transitions team, providing personalised benefits advice and support to people in their own homes and communities across West Devon and Torridge. You will help people understand and access the benefits they are entitled to, maximise their household income and navigate what can often be complex and challenging benefit processes. Many of the people we support face barriers to accessing mainstream services, so the ability to build trust, listen and provide patient, practical support is at the heart of this role. We are looking for someone with strong communication and interpersonal skills, a person-centred approach and a genuine commitment to supporting people experiencing vulnerability or financial hardship. Previous benefits advice experience would be an advantage, but we also welcome applications from people with transferable skills and the right values and aptitude to develop in the role. Full training, support and opportunities for professional development will be provided About the Role Working as part of the Transitions Project, you will provide specialist, person-centred benefits advice to people in their own homes and community settings across West Devon and Torridge. Many of the people we support experience barriers that make it difficult for them to access mainstream advice services, including poor physical or mental health, disability, rural isolation, digital exclusion, low confidence and complex personal circumstances. You will take advice directly to clients, providing the time, flexibility and practical support they need to understand and access their benefit entitlements. You will complete comprehensive benefit checks, support clients to make and manage claims, identify opportunities to maximise household income and help resolve benefit-related problems. This may include supporting clients with challenging decisions, mandatory reconsiderations and appeals, as well as liaising and advocating with the DWP, local authorities and other agencies. The role involves regular lone working and travel to clients' homes, so you will need to be confident working independently while remaining closely connected to the wider Transitions team. This is a rewarding role with the opportunity to make a tangible difference to the financial stability and wellbeing of people who may otherwise struggle to access the support they need.
item.dc:creator: Navigate

item.title: Director of Retail
item.description: Contract: Permanent Hours: 35 hours Salary: Up to £75,000 per annum Location: Flexible with regular travel across our retail network and to London Benefits include but not limited to: -36 days' annual leave inclusive of flexible bank holidays, increasing with length of service -Provision to buy additional annual leave -Enhanced maternity/paternity leave -We match up to 8% pension -Free counselling service -Opportunities to develop and widen your skills -2 days of paid volunteering time per annum to support another part of the organisation About us: The Children's Society has been helping children and young people in this country for over 140 years. We deliver essential local services that provide safe, trusted support to children and young people during times of significant need. Our Social Impact domain is built on shared values, diverse perspectives, and a flexible, people-first approach. We work as one team, building strong relationships across the organisation to drive meaningful change for children and young people. With trust, wellbeing, and collaboration at the heart of how we work, you'll join a culture that supports you to make a real and lasting difference, helping us move closer to our mission of improving the lives of children and young people. About the role: The Children's Society is seeking an innovative and ambitious Retail Director who can reshape our retail portfolio to deliver greater income and impact to support children and young people. You'll play a critical leadership role during a period of transition and opportunity. You'll provide strategic oversight and operational leadership across our national retail network, supporting performance, safeguarding, and team wellbeing while preparing the function for transformation and growth. Representing retail at senior leadership level and working closely with the Executive Director of Marketing and Income Generation, the Director of Retail will deliver the new retail strategy and ensure the function is ready to thrive. To be successful in this role, you will have: -Substantial experience in charity retail leadership, ideally including interim or transitional roles -Proven ability to lead large, dispersed teams through change with confidence and credibility -Strong strategic and commercial acumen, with a track record of driving performance and growth -Experience in safeguarding oversight and compliance across retail operations -Excellent communication, influencing and stakeholder engagement skills Closing date: Midnight on 13th September 2026Interview dates: Week commencing 28th September The Children's Society is committed to safeguarding and protection of the children and young people we work with. As such, our safer recruitment process includes a Basic or Enhanced DBS check, 2 years of references, and additional vetting checks relevant to the role. We have a comprehensive range of policies and procedures in place to promote safeguarding and safer working practices across all areas of our organisation.In support of our commitment to diversity and inclusion, shortlisting is carried out on an anonymised basis. Personal details are hidden from the shortlisting panel, and candidates are referenced by a candidate number only. As part of this process, we ask that your CV is anonymised before submission - this means removing personal information such as your name, contact details, age, and any other identifying details. AI tools can support your application but only when used appropriately. You're welcome to use them to improve clarity, structure, and research. However, overuse or misuse (e.g. inventing experience or using AI during assessments) may lead to rejection at any stage. We want to hear the real you - authenticity matters.
